stories.title: $1.044M for First Responder Mental Health Initiative
stories.summary: Funds will be awarded to Frontline Strong Together to support a statewide initiative for police officers, firefighters, EMS personnel, correctional officers, 9-1-1 dispatchers, and their families.

stories.summary: Funds will support a 'three-share model' health coverage program for low-income workers, with costs shared between businesses, workers, and the public through Access Health.

stories.title: $1.5M Allocated to Lenawee Now Foundation for Workforce Development
stories.summary: The Lenawee Now Foundation will receive $1.5 million to support workforce development programs in the region. The funding aims to address local employment and skill development needs.

stories.title: $1.5M Awarded to Target Alpena Development Corporation for Workforce Housing
stories.summary: Target Alpena Development Corporation in Alpena County will receive $1.5 million to support workforce housing, grant assistance, and small business infrastructure development. The funds aim to boost local economic growth.

stories.title: $1.5M for FQHC Workforce Training
stories.summary: Funds will partner with the Michigan Primary Care Association to provide recruitment and training for FQHC staff, including clinical experience and apprenticeships for underserved communities.

stories.title: $1.975M for Child Caring Institution Infrastructure
stories.summary: Funds will be distributed as grants for capital improvements at licensed child caring institutions, reimbursing costs from property damage or injury caused by youth, with a $100,000 per facility cap.

stories.title: 1 hospitalized after reported explosion at building on Detroit’s west side
stories.summary: A 79-year-old man was hospitalized in critical condition after a reported explosion at a commercial building on Detroit’s west side. Firefighters responded to Northlawn Street near Plymouth Road, extinguishing a small fire and finding the man with severe burns from chemical work. Two other employees were present but unharmed.

photo.alt: 1 hospitalized after reported explosion at building on Detroit’s west side

stories.title: 10 Ways to Combat Loneliness in Ann Arbor
stories.summary: The article provides 10 practical ways to combat loneliness in the Ann Arbor community.

photo.alt: 10 Ways to Combat Loneliness in Ann Arbor

stories.title: $100,000 Customer Satisfaction Survey Program
stories.summary: The state will allocate $100,000 to measure and improve customer satisfaction across service platforms like online transactions and call centers. The department may partner with external entities for survey design, data integration, and performance benchmarking, with a status report due by September 30.

stories.title: $10M invested to research soundwave cancer treatments at the University of Michigan
stories.summary: The University of Michigan has established a $10 million Histotripsy Center to advance non-invasive cancer treatments using soundwaves. The technique, FDA-approved for liver tumors, uses targeted soundwaves to break apart tumors without surgery, radiation, or chemotherapy. Co-inventor Zhen Xu highlights the center's role in expanding research and clinical applications for various cancers and diseases.

photo.alt: Zhen Xu, co-inventor of histotripsy, at the University of Michigan Histotripsy Center opening ceremony. Photo: Brenda Ahearn/University of Michigan, College of Engineering, Communications and Marketing

stories.title: $11.4 Million in Funds Allocated to Create Primary Care Residency Slots by 2031
stories.summary: Unexpended funds up to $11.4 million will be used to create new primary care residency slots in underserved communities, with a work project completion date of September 30, 2031, and a total estimated cost of $22.8 million.

stories.title: 11-year-old shot in face by another child in Detroit; Police Chief Todd Bettison urges gun safety
stories.summary: An 11-year-old was critically injured after being shot in the face by another child inside a home on Detroit’s west side. Police believe an unsecured handgun was involved, and three children, ages 11, 9, and 4, were home alone during the incident.

photo.alt: 11-year-old shot in face by another child in Detroit; Police Chief Todd Bettison urges gun safety

stories.title: 11-year-old shot on Detroit's west side
stories.summary: An 11-year-old boy was shot on Detroit’s west side on October 7, 2026, near Artesian Street and Tireman Avenue. Police are expected to provide an update at 4 p.m., and a person was seen being arrested at the scene, though it is unclear if the arrest is connected to the shooting. The severity of the child’s injuries remains unknown.

photo.alt: An 11-year-old boy was shot in the area of Artesian Street and Tireman Avenue on Detroit's west side on Wednesday, Oct. 7. (WDIV)

stories.title: 12 ways Ann Arbor plans to divide and spend millions from downtown property sale
stories.summary: Ann Arbor City Council has approved a spending plan for the $14.2 million to $17.4 million expected from the sale of the city-owned Kline’s lot. The funds will be allocated to 12 different projects, including affordable housing, sustainable energy initiatives, and infrastructure improvements. The sale is expected to close in 2027, with the final amount depending on the number of housing units developed.

photo.alt: The city-owned Kline's lot off Ashley and William streets in downtown Ann Arbor on Sept. 8, 2026 (Ryan Stanton | MLive.com)

stories.title: 13-year-old boy accused of stealing multiple cars again, breaking into businesses in Oakland County
stories.summary: A 13-year-old boy is facing accusations of stealing multiple vehicles and breaking into businesses across Oakland County. The incidents have raised concerns in the local community, with authorities investigating the case.

photo.alt: 13-year-old boy accused of stealing multiple cars again, breaking into businesses in Oakland County

stories.title: 15 years of household flu data may be one giant leap for prevention
stories.summary: A 15-year study of household flu data from the University of Michigan may significantly advance flu prevention efforts. The research, published on October 1, 2026, could lead to more effective strategies for reducing flu transmission within families. The study's findings are highlighted as a major step forward in public health.

photo.alt: 15 years of household flu data may be one giant leap for prevention

stories.title: 16-year-old hospitalized after Kalamazoo shooting Monday, police say
stories.summary: A 16-year-old boy was hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries after a reported shooting near a residential complex in northwestern Kalamazoo. Police responded to the 1300 block of Fox Ridge Road, urging passers-by to avoid the area, but further details were unavailable Monday night.

photo.alt: A file photo of a Kalamazoo Department of Public Safety vehicle as officers respond to a call in the city.

stories.title: 18-year-old fatally shot on Detroit’s east side overnight
stories.summary: An 18-year-old man was fatally shot early Friday morning on Detroit’s east side. Police responded to a ShotSpotter alert at Cheshire and Moross streets, where the victim succumbed to his injuries. Authorities are seeking public tips to aid the investigation.

photo.alt: 18-year-old fatally shot on Detroit’s east side overnight

stories.title: 19 states poised to make daylight saving time permanent: Are we closer to that happening?
stories.summary: Nineteen states are poised to do away with the twice-yearly time change if Congress moves ahead with the Sunshine Protection Act. However, permanent daylight saving time is unlikely to become law before the Nov. 1 deadline when the U.S. falls back to standard time.

photo.alt: 19 states poised to make daylight saving time permanent: Are we closer to that happening?

stories.title: 19-year-old charged in crash that killed Uber driver, injured passenger in Oak Park
stories.summary: Tracy Darwin Sutton, 19, was charged after allegedly driving through a traffic light in Oak Park, causing a crash that killed an Uber driver and injured a passenger. The incident occurred on September 17, with Sutton found intoxicated. The Uber driver died in the hospital, while the 23-year-old passenger remains in critical condition. Sutton was arraigned on September 20 with a $2 million bond and is scheduled for a court appearance on September 28.

photo.alt: 19-year-old charged in crash that killed Uber driver, injured passenger in Oak Park

stories.title: 1936: Court plaintiff sees double, charges dismissed
stories.summary: In 1936, a robbery case collapsed when the victim couldn’t identify which of two identical twins was the suspect. The twins’ identical appearance led to the dismissal of charges.

photo.alt: 1936: Court plaintiff sees double, charges dismissed

stories.title: 1981: Preservation group fights WSU demolition of historic buildings
stories.summary: In 1981, Wayne State University planned to demolish seven historic buildings, including the Armstrong House. Preservationists argued the structures could be renovated, but the demolition proceeded despite opposition.

photo.alt: Outlier Media newsletter image

stories.title: $1M Allocated to Michigan State University for Agricultural Resiliency Program
stories.summary: Michigan State University’s College of Agriculture and Natural Resources will receive $1 million for the Agricultural Resiliency Program. The funding supports initiatives to strengthen agricultural sustainability and resilience.

stories.title: $1M for Medicaid Outreach and Kidney Disease Prevention
stories.summary: Funds will support outreach by the National Kidney Foundation of Michigan to prevent chronic kidney disease in high-risk populations through the Morris Hood III Initiative.

stories.title: 1st Friday Focus on the Environment: Senator Sarah Anthony gives her thoughts on the environmental aspects of Michigan's next state budget
stories.summary: Senator Sarah Anthony discusses the need for Michigan's next state budget to prioritize water infrastructure and environmental justice, emphasizing bipartisan collaboration and addressing low tipping fees. She highlights the importance of ensuring clean water access across the state and overcoming political challenges to secure funding.

photo.alt: Rebekah Warren

stories.title: $2.2 million in city funds to help 1,000 more Detroit kids access after-school programs
stories.summary: Detroit's GOAL Line after-school program is expanding to seven new sites with city funding, aiming to provide 57 enrichment activities to 1,000 more students. The nonprofit, created in 2018, now operates at multiple community centers and libraries across the city.

photo.alt: $2.2 million in city funds to help 1,000 more Detroit kids access after-school programs

stories.title: $2.2 million in city funds to help 1,000 more Detroit kids access after-school programs
stories.summary: Detroit will open seven new after-school program sites with $2.2 million in city funding, expanding access for 1,000 additional students. Existing sites include recreation centers, libraries, and schools across the city.

photo.alt: $2.2 million in city funds to help 1,000 more Detroit kids access after-school programs

stories.title: $2.5 Million for Dental Hygiene Program at North Central Michigan College
stories.summary: Funds must be awarded to North Central Michigan College to support the purchase of a facility for a new dental hygiene program.

stories.title: 2 charged in connection with deadly ambush shooting in Waterford Township
stories.summary: Two men, Ian Andewla Wells, 18, and Gavin Carl Ort, 19, have been charged in connection with an ambush shooting that left one man dead in Waterford Township. The shooting occurred on Sept. 15 when four men were ambushed by individuals with assault rifles at a pre-arranged meeting location. Wells faces second-degree murder and other charges, while Ort was charged as an accessory after the fact.

photo.alt: Ian Andewla Wells (left) and Gavin Carl Ort (right) (Oakland County Jail)

stories.title: 2 men charged in separate Kalamazoo killings
stories.summary: Two men were charged in two separate killings in Kalamazoo, Michigan, which occurred one day apart on Sept. 27 and 28. Cedric Martin Gunn, 18, and Markeet McKinley Primer Jr., 20, face murder charges and other offenses, with investigators suggesting the second killing was in retaliation for the first. Both were denied bond and have scheduled court appearances in October.

photo.alt: A crime lab at the scene of an incident in Kalamazoo. Brad Devereaux MLive

stories.title: $2 Million for St. Louis Center Capital Improvements
stories.summary: Funds must be awarded to the St. Louis Center to support capital improvements at the facility.

stories.title: 2 Ole Miss students dead, officials urge caution
stories.summary: Two Ole Miss students are dead, and law enforcement officials are running separate investigations. The identities of the students are being withheld, and the causes of the deaths remain under investigation. Officials urge caution regarding substances like Kratom, though no evidence links it to the deaths.

photo.alt: Police investigating the deaths of two Ole Miss students

stories.title: 20,000 mail-in ballots received by the city less than a month before election
stories.summary: Detroit election officials report that approximately 20,000 absentee ballots have been returned with less than a month remaining before the November election. The city mailed 100,000 absentee ballots between September 19 and 24, and 38 drop boxes are available citywide to facilitate voting.

photo.alt: 20,000 mail-in ballots received by the city less than a month before election

stories.title: 2026 Detroit school board election explainer: What’s at stake for students and families?
stories.summary: The 2026 Detroit school board election could bring heightened conflict with district leadership, as concerns grow over potential tensions between a new board and Superintendent Nikolai Vitti. Historical precedents show board changes often lead to criticism or efforts to remove administrators, though Vitti’s nine-year tenure in Detroit has been relatively stable compared to past years. His contract expires in 2028, and he has previously hinted at plans to leave the district.

photo.alt: 2026 Detroit school board election explainer: What’s at stake for students and families?

stories.title: 2026 Detroit school board election explainer: What’s at stake for students and families?
stories.summary: Detroit parents and community members are calling for a new school board to challenge the status quo, with some advocating for faster academic progress and new curricula while others emphasize accountability and raising educational standards. The upcoming November election will determine five board seats, including one with a partial term ending in 2028.

photo.alt: 2026 Detroit school board election explainer: What’s at stake for students and families?

stories.title: 2026 Detroit school board election explainer: What’s at stake for students and families?
stories.summary: The upcoming 2026 Detroit school board election could lead to increased conflict between the new board and district leadership, including Superintendent Nikolai Vitti. Past instances of board-superintendent tensions, such as Vitti's departure from Florida's Duval County Public Schools, raise concerns about potential instability. The board's role in holding the district accountable and the possibility of Vitti's contract expiration in 2028 are key factors in the discussion.

photo.alt: 2026 Detroit school board election explainer: What’s at stake for students and families?

stories.title: 2027 Budget Discussion – Expenditures (Capital Projects)
stories.summary: The board discussed capital expenditures, including plans to partner with Canton Township on EV charging stations. Marian Nicholson confirmed the library is still budgeting for the project but awaiting township action.

stories.title: 2027 Budget Discussion – Revenues
stories.summary: The library projects a budget increase for 2027 despite the Headlee reduction, recommending budgeting for the full $1.4088 mills with a 99% collection rate. E. Davis highlighted market increases and new developments as factors.

stories.title: $210,000 for Mobile Mental Health Crisis Unit in Jackson-Hillsdale
stories.summary: Funds must be awarded to Jackson-Hillsdale Community Mental Health Board to purchase an innovative mobile mental health crisis unit.

stories.title: 29-year-old ‘endangered’ woman located safely at Southfield hospital
stories.summary: Christian Cook, a 29-year-old Southfield woman reported missing since Sept. 13, has been located safely at a local hospital, police said. Southfield Police Department confirmed she is receiving appropriate medical care, and authorities thanked the community for their assistance during the search. Search efforts involving drones, K-9 units, and rescue teams were suspended on Sept. 16 after no further signs of Cook were found.

photo.alt: Christian Cook located safely at Southfield hospital

stories.title: $2M Awarded to Escanaba for Road Infrastructure Projects
stories.summary: The city of Escanaba in Delta County will receive $2 million for road infrastructure projects. The funds will be used to improve transportation infrastructure and road conditions.

stories.title: 3 dead after boat crashes, capsizes near MacRay Harbor in Lake St. Clair
stories.summary: Three people have died following a boat crash in Lake St. Clair near MacRay Harbor in Harrison Township. The Macomb County Sheriff’s Office received a 911 call around 10:48 p.m. after a passenger swam to shore, reporting the crash occurred around 8 p.m. and the boat capsized. Marine teams recovered three bodies from the submerged vessel overnight, and an investigation is ongoing.

photo.alt: Fatal boat crash scene in Lake St. Clair

stories.title: 3 Metro Detroit communities mailing out new absentee ballots due to error
stories.summary: New absentee ballots are being sent to voters in three Wayne County communities after an error in the ballot printing process. The error, discovered four days after ballots were mailed on Sept. 24, affects Van Buren Township, Sumpter Township, and Belleville. Election officials attribute the issue to an omission in the Belleville Area District Library Board portion of the ballot.

photo.alt: 3 Metro Detroit communities mailing out new absentee ballots due to error

stories.title: 3 people found on overturned sailboat in Lake Michigan
stories.summary: Three boaters were rescued after their 16-foot catamaran capsized in Lake Michigan near Coloma. The U.S. Coast Guard and Berrien County Sheriff’s Office rescued the three individuals, who were wearing life jackets and holding onto the overturned boat. The incident occurred on Sept. 21, with the Coast Guard emphasizing the importance of safety gear and preparedness.

photo.alt: Lake Michigan boat rescue

stories.title: 3 rescued after boat overturns on Lake Michigan near Coloma
stories.summary: The Coast Guard and Berrien County Sheriff’s Office rescued three boaters whose catamaran capsized offshore Roadside Park near Coloma, Michigan, on Sept. 21. All three were wearing life jackets and were rescued after being located by drone operators. The Coast Guard emphasized the importance of safety gear and preparedness during the incident.

photo.alt: Portrait of Dan Basso

stories.title: 3 running for 2 seats on Bay City school board
stories.summary: Three candidates are competing for two nonpartisan seats on the Bay City Public Schools Board of Education. The candidates include a retired teacher, a former board member, and a community member with young children in the district. The election is set for November 3, 2026.

photo.alt: Bay City Public Schools Joey Oliver | MLive.com

stories.title: 31st annual Earthfest highlights campus sustainability, promotes circular economy
stories.summary: The 31st annual Earthfest, hosted by the University of Michigan's Office of Campus Sustainability and Innovation and other departments, featured over 40 programs and organizations promoting sustainability. Attendees participated in activities like the Repair Cafe, collected prizes from campus farms, and learned about climate initiatives during Climate Week. The event emphasized circular economy principles and engaged students, faculty, and community partners.

photo.alt: Matthew Darnell, Leslie Science and Nature Center program coordinator, demonstrates a snake to students during Earthfest on the Diag Thursday afternoon. Zoe Wang/DAILY.

stories.title: 34-year-old Chipotle worker fatally stabbed on lunch break in downtown Detroit
stories.summary: A 34-year-old mother, Jaquoya Wix, was fatally stabbed in an unprovoked attack while on a lunch break at a downtown Detroit Chipotle restaurant. The suspect, a man in his 40s with severe mental health issues, was apprehended 20 minutes later. Wix’s family has launched a fundraiser to support her 15-year-old daughter, and Chipotle expressed condolences for the tragedy.

photo.alt: Police lights

stories.title: 34-year-old woman fatally stabbed while on lunch break in downtown Detroit identified
stories.summary: The 34-year-old woman fatally stabbed on September 20, 2026 while on a lunch break in downtown Detroit has been identified as Jaquoya Wix. The suspect is in custody, and witnesses described the random attack that occurred near Woodward Avenue and E. Congress Street. The victim's family has set up a GoFundMe for funeral expenses and to support her 15-year-old daughter.

photo.alt: Jaquoya Wix, 34, fatally stabbed in downtown Detroit

stories.title: 36,600 Michigan students face homelessness. Experts say addressing poverty is key to improving literacy.
stories.summary: Experts argue that poverty must be addressed to improve literacy outcomes for Michigan's 36,600 homeless students. The state's education candidates are urged to prioritize this issue.

stories.title: 38 horses seized from Milford business, owner disputes claims
stories.summary: The owner of High Vibe Trail Rides, Lucie Ptasznik, disputes allegations of animal neglect after 38 horses were seized. Her boyfriend, Jason Roberts, claims independent veterinary evaluations and animal control reports show the horses were in good condition, and attributes the campaign against her to former employees with personal grievances. Roberts also denied the authenticity of online photos showing horses in poor condition.

photo.alt: 38 horses seized from Milford business, owner disputes claims

stories.summary: The Bureau of Professional Licensing will allocate at least $400,000 to the Michigan Realtors Association to support real estate continuing education approval and tracking in the state.

stories.summary: A renovated dog park in Saugatuck Township, Michigan, is reopening after $160,000 in improvements. The Tails N' Trails Dog Park, featuring 39.5 acres of trails including a 5-acre fenced area, will host a reopening event on Sept. 24. Renovations funded by the township parks millage enhanced accessibility and usability.

stories.summary: The Eastern Echo reports that five candidates are running unopposed for the Ypsilanti District Library Board of Trustees. Kerri Pepperman, a 26-year Ypsilanti resident with a background in web development and a University of Michigan master's degree, is one of the candidates. She joined the library's fundraising committee after seeking ways to get involved, strengthening her ties to the library and its staff.

stories.summary: Funds will be allocated as grants to qualified providers to assist residents with water utility bills, service restoration, and affordability plans. Qualified providers must report outcomes by September 30 of the fiscal year.

stories.summary: The state will allocate $50,000 from foster care funds as a competitive grant to provide essential items like clothing, toys, and school supplies to local foster children and their families free of charge.

stories.title: 50,000 Volkswagen drivers warned their vehicle may stall over a software issue: What to know
stories.summary: Volkswagen is recalling 49,958 2025 Tiguan vehicles due to a software defect that can cause the body control module to reset, leading to engine stalling and loss of critical vehicle functions. The recall addresses non-compliance with federal safety standards, though no injuries or crashes have been reported. Volkswagen will provide free software updates to affected owners, with notifications beginning November 6.

photo.alt: Volkswagen

stories.summary: The Arab American National Museum will receive $500,000 in funding from the state's legislatively directed spending items. The allocation supports the museum's operations and cultural initiatives.

stories.summary: The Zekelman Holocaust Center will receive $500,000 in state funding to support its educational and commemorative programs. This allocation helps preserve Holocaust history and promote awareness.

stories.summary: The Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History has been allocated $500,000 from the state's budget. This funding supports the museum's mission to preserve and showcase African American history and culture.

stories.summary: The state will allocate $500,000 to the Adoptive Family Support Network by December 1 to expand its mentor program for adoptive parents. A report on program outcomes, including cases prevented from out-of-home placement, must be submitted by March 1.

stories.summary: Funds must be awarded to IM Kids 3rd Meal in Ionia County to secure and equip a permanent facility for the program.

stories.title: 56% of Michigan teachers are thinking about leaving in five years, poll says
stories.summary: A new poll reveals that 25% of Michigan teachers are considering leaving the profession within a year, while 56% may exit within five years. The survey, commissioned by the Michigan Educator Workforce Initiative, highlights concerns over inadequate compensation, insufficient training for new teachers, and barriers to classroom innovation as key reasons for potential departures.

photo.alt: New poll results show 25% of Michigan teachers say they are strongly considering teaching in the next 12 months, while 56% say they're considering exiting in the next five years.

stories.title: $5M University of Michigan grant aimed at business students advocating for climate
stories.summary: The University of Michigan has received a $4.9 million grant from the Erb Institute to support graduate students pursuing dual degrees in business and environmental sustainability. The scholarship, effective for a decade, offers up to $40,000 annually for new admits and $25,000 for mid-year admits, aiming to alleviate financial burdens and foster sustainable business practices.

photo.alt: Mariana Lopes speaking at the Erb 30th anniversary event. Image credit: University of Michigan.

stories.title: 6 things to know about massive plastics factory fire, fallout in South Haven
stories.summary: The City of South Haven and South Haven Area Emergency Services are addressing the aftermath of a 14-hour fire at East Jordan Plastics that caused a citywide power outage, canceled community events, and prompted an EPA response. The fire began at 3:48 p.m. on September 29, 2026, triggering multiple alarms and dark smoke over the area.

photo.alt: East Jordan Plastics fire in South Haven

stories.title: $615,600 Awarded to Michigan’s Military Heritage Museum for Facility Expansion
stories.summary: Michigan’s Military Heritage Museum in Jackson County will receive $615,600 for facility expansion, modernization of exhibits, and new features. The funds will enhance the museum's ability to showcase military history.

stories.title: 67 Detroit residents receive home deeds through Buy Back Program
stories.summary: Sixty-seven Detroit residents got the deeds to homes they had been living in and seeking ownership of through the Buy Back Program of the Detroit Land Bank Authority (DLBA). The hurdles to ownership included paying property taxes in full, along with committing to and completing financial literacy counseling and attending homeownership workshops.

stories.summary: $800,000 is allocated to the Prosecuting Attorneys Coordinating Council for central administrative services including human resources, budgeting, technology, and legal support following the council's transfer.

stories.summary: The Village of Clarkston in Oakland County will receive $834,400 to improve walkability and pedestrian safety. The funds will be used for infrastructure upgrades to enhance community accessibility.

stories.title: 8ball & MJG, Bun B And The Renaissance Orchestra Coming To Fox Theatre On Saturday, April 24
stories.summary: 8ball & MJG, Bun B, and The Renaissance Orchestra will perform at the Fox Theatre in Detroit on Saturday, April 24, 2026. The event is part of the Spring 2026 lineup announced by 313 Presents.

stories.title: 9 Michigan Indigenous communities receive $479K to reshape Native curricula, imagery
stories.summary: Nine Michigan Indigenous communities received $479,988.38 in funding from the Native American Heritage Fund (NAHF) to support accurate Indigenous representation, expand tribal curricula, and replace offensive imagery in schools and institutions. The grants, awarded during a ceremony at Firekeeper’s Casino in Battle Creek, aim to promote positive relationships and educate about Indigenous history and sovereignty. Recipients include school districts, cultural organizations, and historical societies working on curriculum development, cultural exchanges, and tribal-led projects.

photo.alt: Darrel Delabreau and his son perform at the Nottawaseppi Huron Band of Potawatomi’s annual Pow Wow on June 23, 2024, on the Pine Creek Indian Reservation in Fulton, Michigan.

stories.title: A 1947 Michigan sweet shop is being foreclosed over unpaid debt, owner claims retaliation
stories.summary: A Southwest Michigan sweet shop building will go to a sheriff’s sale auction on Sept. 24 as the city moves to foreclose over an unpaid debt. Owner Tom Hitchcock disputes the debt, alleging the city reversed loan terms and claims the action is retaliation for a civil rights lawsuit against the city.

photo.alt: Inside of Cafe Italiano in Buchanan. The sweet shop, which opened in 1947, is facing foreclosure over an unpaid debt.(Provided by Tom Hitchcock)

stories.title: A Data Center on the Huron River: Ypsilanti Township Pushes Back

Residents and local officials have raised concerns about environmental impact, water and energy use, and the lack of transparency in the project's planning. The proposal, which will appear as City Proposal E on the November 3 ballot, would establish a public utility board to oversee a potential shift from DTE Energy. A2P2 argues for local accountability, while A2REC warns of risks from non-expert governance and workforce challenges.

stories.title: Ann Arbor for Public Power’s ballot proposal will be in voters’ hands in November — here’s what to know
stories.summary: Ann Arbor for Public Power successfully gathered over 5,000 signatures to place a proposal on the 2026 midterm ballot, aiming to replace DTE Energy’s electrical utility with a city-run power grid. If approved on Nov. 3, a public utility board would be elected by 2028 to oversee the transition. The proposal faces opposition from DTE-funded groups, but court challenges to block it have been dismissed. Supporters argue for democratic control of utilities, while critics raise concerns about costs and grid reliability.

stories.title: Ann Arbor for Public Power’s ballot proposal will be in voters’ hands in November — here’s what to know

stories.title: Citizens-only voting petition sponsors look to 2028 after initiative fails before state canvassers
stories.summary: Sponsors of a Michigan ballot initiative to implement citizen-only voting and voter ID requirements failed to qualify the measure for the 2026 ballot due to insufficient valid signatures. After losing appeals in both the U.S. and Michigan Supreme Courts, organizers plan to resubmit the petition in 2028 with improved signature collection. Election officials and legal experts dismissed claims of procedural bias, emphasizing the initiative fell short of required validity thresholds.

stories.title: Citizens Research Council outlines impacts of Mop Up Michigan initiative
stories.summary: The Mop Up Michigan Initiative (Proposal 2) seeks to ban political contributions from government contractors, regulated utilities, and related entities to state and local candidates. The Citizens Research Council of Michigan released a report analyzing the proposal's potential impacts, including increased transparency, legal challenges under the First Amendment, and possible effects on contractor participation and utility spending. The initiative faces constitutional questions about the scope of its restrictions and the justification for targeting specific industries.

stories.title: Citizens Research Council outlines impacts of Mop Up Michigan initiative

stories.title: Community
stories.summary: Give me your tired, your poor, your huddled masses yearning to breathe free. At Greendale Community College, all are accepted and all have a bright future ahead of them. Have you ever felt nervous to deliver a class presentation in front of dozens of strangers? Have you ever been humbled by what you thought would be a blowoff class? Have you ever been helpless to stop petty bickering between close friends? There’s a “Community” episode for each of these issues, and many more. The show captured viewers’ attention with ambitious outings, like “[Modern Warfare](https://youtu.be/XcOG5iZpV-k?si=7RcOVN8nPRSMI8Va)” (a paintball competition set entirely at the college) and “[Remedial Chaos Theory](https://youtu.be/POT3plx0vBs?si=bwUHzhUT4ThVsHjt)” (a timeline-hopping adventure of what-ifs). But in its golden years — specifically Seasons 1-3 — “Community” thrived on its warm relatability and sympathy for a band of misfits [bound together](https://youtu.be/aznTfytzNQ4?si=UXdGH1eh7y_7D85K) by [mutual](https://youtu.be/q44WaM5Rm6A?si=3vzWloDJtpF5duut) [lunacy](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dlXuJpuk6oA): the “Study Group.’’ The members of the group are all at different stages of life, but ultimately seeking the same thing: a raw, unadulterated college experience and all the insight it might bring. “Community” is anchored by inventive, witty sitcom writing and a set of comedic powerhouses delivering career-best performances. If you’re in college, there’s never been a better time to watch it.

photo.alt: Courtesy of Ana Torresarpi

stories.title: Deadline for clerks to submit notice to process AV ballots before Election Day

stories.title: Deadline for notice of temporary polling place changes
stories.summary: Notice of temporary changes to polling place locations must be provided by Tuesday, October 13, 2026. This requirement is specified in section 168.662 of the election regulations.

stories.title: Deadline for public logic and accuracy test of early voting equipment
stories.summary: The public logic and accuracy test of early voting equipment must be conducted by Monday, October 19, 2026. If early voting starts before the required date, the deadline shifts back to five days before the start of early voting, as per sections 168.720j and R 168.778.

stories.title: Deadline to post notice of AV counting place details
stories.summary: County clerks must post notice on their website and in their office about the location, dates, hours, and number of election inspectors for absent voter (AV) counting places by Friday, October 16, 2026. stories.title: Deadline to Publish Election Notice for August-November 2026 Elections

stories.title: Deadline to update Qualified Voter File for deceased individuals

stories.summary: Detroit City Council Member Gabriela Santiago-Romero emphasizes accessibility, cultural programming, and community access for Fort Wayne's revitalization. stories.summary: Detroit City Council Member Gabriela Santiago-Romero is requesting an 18-month moratorium on AI data centers while the city develops regulations for these facilities. stories.summary: Side Hustle Lounge in downtown Detroit has transformed into the 'Haunted House of Film' for a monthlong Halloween takeover featuring horror movie-themed decor and cocktails. stories.title: Detroit community advocates canvass west side neighborhood after deadly shooting

The effort included city officials, violence intervention groups, and residents addressing concerns about crime, junk cars, and abandoned homes. A public listening session is scheduled for Oct. 5 to gather resident input on needed resources.

stories.summary: Detroit Disability Power is hiring a visual artist to expand its reach and create accessible graphics for social media, email, print and online spaces. The full-time position pays a salary of $55,000-$62,000 plus benefits. Apply by Sept. 23.

stories.title: Detroit district catching up to charter schools, 2026 M-STEP results show

stories.summary: Comerica Park, home of the Detroit Tigers, will be renamed Fifth Third Park after Fifth Third Bancorp acquired Comerica Bank. Michigan Regional President Steve Davis emphasized the significance of the park to Detroit's community pride.

stories.summary: Eli Lilly and Company and Planet Harvest are distributing over 1,300 brain-healthy produce boxes to food-insecure seniors in Metro Detroit on World Alzheimer’s Day. The boxes include apples, cabbage, cucumbers, collard greens, lemons, oranges, corn, and zucchinis. Seniors can pick up boxes at locations like Rochester Christian University and Webster Community Center, with door-to-door distributions at senior living homes.

stories.summary: The citywide coalition MoveDetroit is announcing the first 13 winners of a grant aimed at increasing and stabilizing the city’s population. stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: Kamala Harris endorses Abdul El-Sayed in Detroit
stories.summary: Former Vice President Kamala Harris endorsed Democrat Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate at an event in Detroit. She highlighted his potential as a national voice for the state. stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: MDHHS to award $1.5 million for community violence intervention initiatives
stories.summary: Five organizations, including two in Detroit, will receive $1.5 million in funding from the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS) for community violence intervention programs. The grants aim to reduce firearm violence and its impacts in historically disinvested neighborhoods through public health and safety initiatives. Each recipient will receive $300,000 for a two-year project running from September 1, 2026, to September 30, 2028.

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: Nonprofit LGBT Detroit provides mental health services at new facility on the city’s West side
stories.summary: LGBT Detroit Health, a nonprofit, is opening a new wellness center on Detroit's West side offering mental health services, fitness classes, and chronic care management. The facility provides a safe space for the LGBT community and partners with local health organizations for testing and vaccinations. It is funded through state grants and membership fees.

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: ShotStoppers program significantly decreased gun violence, says University of Michigan report
stories.summary: A University of Michigan analysis found a 45% decrease in homicides and nonfatal shootings in Detroit since the launch of the ShotStoppers community violence intervention program three years ago. The program funds community-based organizations with $175,000 per quarter and performance-based bonuses to reduce gun violence in high-risk areas.

stories.title: Detroit explores alternatives to DTE Energy monopoly
stories.summary: Detroit City Council and Mayor Mary Sheffield's administration are investigating alternatives to DTE Energy's near-monopoly as the city's energy provider. stories.summary: The family of Kimberlly Moore claims her body was accidentally cremated before her scheduled viewing at Hutchison Funeral Home, leading to a demand for answers. The funeral home has launched an internal investigation and stated they will address the issue if found at fault.

stories.title: Detroit Farm and Cider owner sells property after legal disputes
stories.summary: Leandra King, owner of Detroit Farm and Cider, is selling her property for $5.3 million after years of legal disputes with the city over animal possession and code violations. The city recently seized animals from the property.

stories.title: Detroit Fire Battalion Chief charged after alleged road rage attack in Livonia
stories.summary: A Detroit Fire Department Battalion Chief, Thomas Suchora, was charged with assault and malicious destruction of property after allegedly attacking 64-year-old Todd Richards during a road rage incident in Livonia on Aug. 25. Suchora, who has been with the department since 1995, was placed on unpaid leave following the Sept. 9 criminal charges and is scheduled for a preliminary hearing on Oct. 8. Richards, who has a pacemaker and is awaiting a kidney transplant, plans to file a civil lawsuit over the destruction of his $1,200 phone and injuries sustained.

stories.title: Detroit Lions’ Jameson Williams won’t face charges following alleged domestic violence investigation
stories.summary: The Oakland County Prosecutor’s Office announced it will not file charges against Detroit Lions wide receiver Jameson Williams after investigating an alleged domestic violence incident that occurred on August 6 and was reported to Novi police in September. Investigators reviewed evidence including statements, photos, and communications, but concluded there was no cause for charges. Williams’ attorneys denied the allegations, stating the claims are baseless.

stories.title: Detroit man arrested in August shooting at Oakland County park
stories.summary: A Detroit man has been arrested more than a month after he allegedly shot a man at a park in Oakland County. Ruben Aleman Contreras faces six felony charges, including assault with intent to murder and possession of a firearm by a prohibited person. The incident occurred on August 23 at Jaycee Park in Pontiac, leaving the victim with gunshot wounds to the abdomen and right buttock.

stories.title: Detroit man charged with murder after deadly Warren flea market refund dispute

Prosecutors allege Johnson assaulted a man and then drove his van into his brother, killing him. Johnson faces charges including first-degree murder and felony offenses involving a motor vehicle.

photo.alt: Detroit man charged with murder after deadly Warren flea market refund dispute

stories.title: Detroit man charged with murder in ‘random’ stabbing of Chipotle worker
stories.summary: A 42-year-old Detroit man, Devon Jason Watson, has been charged with first-degree murder in the fatal stabbing of 34-year-old Chipotle employee Jaquoya Wix. Prosecutors described the attack as random but premeditated. Watson and Wix did not know each other, and the stabbing occurred in an alley behind a downtown Detroit restaurant on Sept. 20, 2026.

Sterling Anthony Peters was given a $50,000 bond and ordered to remain under house arrest following his arraignment on Oct. 8, 2026. The incidents occurred on Oct. 5 at two Detroit government buildings, with prosecutors describing the threats as 'very disturbing' and a growing concern for public officials.

A federal charge of possessing a firearm as a felon was filed after earlier state charges were dismissed due to the victim's absence as a witness.

stories.title: Detroit Public Schools and DFT Reach Tentative Agreement on Class Size Overage Pay for 2026-2028
stories.summary: A tentative agreement between Detroit Public Schools Community District and the Detroit Federation of Teachers outlines new class size overage compensation for the 2026-2027 and 2027-2028 school years. Provisions of the existing DFT collective bargaining agreement remain in effect beyond this letter.

stories.summary: The tentative agreement outlines payment structures for teachers in Detroit Public Schools when class sizes exceed contractual maximums. Payments vary based on the number of students above the limit, with amounts per quarter and annual totals specified. Conditions include mutual acknowledgment of oversized classes and efforts to reduce enrollments.

stories.title: Detroit reports 101 properties damaged after EF-2 tornado
stories.summary: Detroit’s storm response update shows 101 properties damaged by the Sept. 3 EF-2 tornado — the city’s first since 1997 — with the hardest-hit areas including McDougall-Hunt, Islandview, West Village, Indian Village, East Village, Pingree Park and Belle Isle. Mayor Mary Sheffield declared a local state of emergency. Crews removed 295 fallen trees, cleared 83 streets, hauled 342 tons of debris, and restored power to all traffic signals, though full recovery is expected to take time.

stories.title: Detroit school board appoints 25-year-old youth advocate as its newest member
stories.summary: Jeremiah Steen, a 25-year-old philanthropist and youth advocate, was appointed to the Detroit Public Schools Community District board to fill a vacancy left by the death of member Iris Taylor. Steen will serve through December 2026 and aims to focus on workforce development and economic mobility for students. He was selected after scoring highest in a third-party evaluation of candidates.

stories.title: Detroit School Board Election Features 34 Candidates for 5 Seats
stories.summary: The Detroit Public School Community District school board election will see 34 candidates competing for five open seats. Only 19 of the 34 candidates responded to Chalkbeat Detroit's outreach about their priorities and views on district challenges. Voters will choose among them on November 3.

stories.title: Detroit school board must fill open seat ahead of November election
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) school board must fill an open seat before the November election. Potential applicants include LaTasha Butler, who was the fourth highest vote-getter in the 2024 election and recently left her role as senior vice president and executive director of City Year Detroit. The dates for upcoming interviews have not yet been publicly posted.

stories.title: Detroit school board reconsiders plans to demolish four closed buildings
stories.summary: The Detroit school board is reconsidering plans to demolish four closed buildings, which would cost nearly $5 million according to a district report. Board member Ida Simmons-Short suggested prioritizing classroom resources over demolition costs and proposed selling the buildings to generate more funds for students. Thurgood Marshall Elementary-Middle School is next on the district’s list of small schools to close in 2027, with 17 more buildings under review for high operating costs due to low enrollment.

stories.title: Detroit school board’s chair and vice chair will not seek reelection in November
stories.summary: Two Detroit school board leaders, LaTrice McClendon and Corletta Vaughn, will not seek reelection in November, citing personal reasons and disqualification due to late fees. Their departure may lead to a significant shift in the district's governance and policies.

photo.alt: DPSCD board chair LaTrice McClendon, left, and vice chair Corletta Vaughn, are not running for reelection. They are shown in a June 2025 meeting reading a statement about a district student who had been detained by federal immigration officials. (Elaine Cromie / Chalkbeat)

stories.title: Detroit school board signals desire to find alternatives to demolition for four closed buildings
stories.summary: The Detroit school board is reconsidering plans to demolish four recently closed schools after community criticism. Originally scheduled for demolition in June 2027, the board is exploring alternatives like selling or leasing the buildings. The four schools closed due to low enrollment and high costs, with demolition estimated to cost nearly $5 million.

photo.alt: Some board members for the Detroit Public Schools Community District are reconsidering plans to demolish four school buildings that closed at the end of the 2025-26 school year. (Elaine Cromie / Chalkbeat)

stories.title: Detroit school board to fill vacant seat of late member Iris Taylor ahead of November election
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District board must fill an open seat left by the recent death of member Iris Taylor before the November election. The board will interview candidates, including the 2024 election runner-up Sherisse Butler, and select an appointee to serve through the end of 2026. State law requires the seat to be filled within 30 days, or it will be assigned by the Wayne Regional Educational Service Agency.

photo.alt: Board members meeting to interview candidates in July 2025 (Elaine Cromie / Chalkbeat)

stories.title: Detroit school district adopts new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) has implemented a new policy restricting unexcused early sign-outs, requiring documentation for pickups and prohibiting early releases in the final 30 minutes of the school day. Parents will face mandatory meetings and attendance contracts if students accumulate multiple unexcused departures, with consequences including chronic absenteeism tracking and grade retention for frequent absences.

photo.alt: Detroit school district adopts new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs

stories.title: Detroit school district adopts new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs
stories.summary: The Detroit school district has adopted a new policy to address unexcused early sign-outs, with parents expressing mixed reactions. While some support protecting instructional time, others raise concerns about socioeconomic barriers and the needs of students with disabilities. The district acknowledges limited research on partial-day absenteeism and its impact on learning.

photo.alt: Detroit school district adopts new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs

stories.title: Detroit school district adopts new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs

Parents expressed mixed reactions, with some supporting the change to protect instructional time and others raising concerns about socioeconomic barriers and students with disabilities. The district highlights the issue similarly to its efforts against chronic absenteeism, though limited research exists on effective solutions for partial-day absences.

photo.alt: Detroit school district adopts new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs

stories.title: Detroit school district and some charters lag behind state
stories.summary: In spring 2026, Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) showed long-term growth in M-STEP proficiency rates but lagged behind statewide averages. Many Detroit charter schools also underperformed compared to the state, though some, like Pembroke Academy, outperformed both the district and state averages in multiple subjects.

stories.title: Detroit school district releases 2026-27 calendar
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District has released its 2026-27 school year calendar, with a start date of Aug. 24 for students. The calendar includes 175 student attendance days and five professional development days for staff, meeting Michigan's 180-day minimum. It does not observe Eid al-Fitr, a Muslim holiday expected on March 10, despite advocacy from students and community members.

stories.title: Detroit students canvass to ask voters to support Proposal S
stories.summary: Detroit students and volunteers with 482Forward are canvassing to promote Proposal S, a school millage on the Aug. 4 primary ballot that would allow Detroit Public Schools Community District to collect its own operating tax. If not approved by July 1, 2027, the district faces an $111 million deficit. The campaign aims to educate voters about the millage, which replaces a previous system and ensures continued funding for schools.

photo.alt: Lindsey Matson, deputy director of youth organizing for 482Forward, explains Proposal S to a voter in Corktown.

stories.title: Detroit superintendent addresses viral criticisms from content creator
stories.summary: The Detroit superintendent addressed viral criticisms from a content creator, stating the district intends to respond legally to baseless information. The discussion included procedures for contractor proposals and efforts to replace contractors with full-time staff, particularly in janitorial roles.

photo.alt: Detroit superintendent addresses viral criticisms from content creator

stories.title: Detroit Tenants Union Lawsuit: Evictions and Compliance
stories.summary: The Detroit Tenants Union lawsuit challenges eviction practices tied to housing compliance, with landlords warning of market collapse due to maintenance costs and tenants arguing safety shouldn't depend on profitability. The next hearing is set for Sept. 21, where a judge may rule on a motion to dismiss the case.

photo.alt: A row of older red-brick-and-wood houses with porches and trees line the street under a gray, overcast sky.

stories.title: Detroit to Receive $1.25M for Right-to-Counsel Eviction Program
stories.summary: The city of Detroit in Wayne County will receive $1.25 million to implement a right-to-counsel program for tenants facing eviction proceedings. This initiative aims to provide legal support to city tenants during eviction processes.

stories.title: Detroit wants more retail in its neighborhoods. Small businesses say they need more foot traffic first.
stories.summary: The Avenue of Fashion is highlighted as a test case for expanding retail in Detroit's neighborhoods. Surrounding areas like Sherwood Forest and Palmer Woods contribute to the corridor's potential, with existing businesses such as Bakers Keyboard Lounge adding to its appeal. Strategies include increasing year-round activity through winter events and holiday shopping to boost foot traffic beyond the summer season.

photo.alt: Detroit wants more retail in its neighborhoods. Small businesses say they need more foot traffic first.

stories.title: Detroit woman accused of accidentally shooting, injuring 13-year-old sister pleads guilty
stories.summary: A 21-year-old Detroit woman, Adriana Arnold, has pleaded guilty to accidentally shooting her 13-year-old sister with an unsecured firearm in the bathroom on August 25, 2026. The incident occurred on Detroit’s west side near Puritan Avenue, and the victim was hospitalized for a gunshot wound to her left arm. Arnold will be sentenced on November 10, 2026.

photo.alt: Detroit woman accused of accidentally shooting, injuring 13-year-old sister pleads guilty

stories.title: Detroit woman facing human trafficking, prostitution charges after victim seeks help from motel housekeeper
stories.summary: A Detroit woman has been charged with operating a human trafficking enterprise in Southfield after an alleged prostitution victim sought help from a motel housekeeper. Prosecutors say the victim was lured into prostitution by Janeice Florence Robinson, 27, and was forced to perform sex acts. The victim approached a housekeeper at the Marvins Garden Inn on Sept. 10, prompting police to be contacted and Robinson to be arrested.

photo.alt: Janeice Florence Robinson, 27, of Detroit, is facing multiple felony charges for allegedly trafficking a woman into prostitution at a Southfield motel.

stories.title: Detroit woman’s basement floods with sewage after city pipe work
stories.summary: Detroit resident Sharon Poindexter has dealt with sewage backing up into her basement since around Sept. 10, coinciding with city crews replacing lead service lines on her street. She says the situation worsens whenever her household uses water and that repeated calls to the city went nowhere. After WXYZ contacted Detroit Water and Sewerage Department, Deputy Director Sam Smalley said crews noticed a sewage smell near the lead line work and sent workers out to investigate and fix the issue.

photo.alt: Detroit woman’s basement floods with sewage after city pipe work

stories.title: Detroit woman sexually exploited, trafficked missing 16-year-old girl, feds say
stories.summary: Federal investigators identified a Detroit woman as the suspect in a case involving the sexual exploitation and trafficking of a missing 16-year-old girl after the victim recognized a tattooed hand in evidence. The woman, in custody, faces federal charges and has a prior criminal record in Wayne and Macomb counties for weapons and drug offenses. She is scheduled to appear in federal court on October 27 for a status conference.

Early voting starts Oct. 24, with the millage also supporting the Belle Isle Nature Center and school programs.

stories.title: DNR, Coast Guard rescue father, son who fell into Lake St. Clair
stories.summary: A father and son were rescued on Sept. 26 after becoming stranded in Lake St. Clair while setting a buoy course for a sailboat race. Both suffered hypothermia when a line tangled their boat's propeller, leading the father to enter the water to untangle it. The son later fell in and called 911, prompting a joint rescue effort by the Michigan DNR and Coast Guard.

photo.alt: Portrait of Jalen Williams

stories.title: DNR commissions new Lake Michigan research vessel
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Natural Resources has commissioned a new 66-foot, steel-hulled research vessel called the RV Steelhead to monitor Lake Michigan's fisheries and aquatic ecosystem. The vessel replaces an older DNR research vessel and includes safety and efficiency upgrades such as improved navigation equipment, a gyrostabilizer, and a solar charging system.

photo.alt: DNR Deputy Director Shannon Lot christens the RV Steelhead on September 30.

stories.title: DNR saves 27 'dinosaur fish' trapped in river. How they rescued sturgeon
stories.summary: Michigan Department of Natural Resources staff rescued 27 lake sturgeon stranded by low-water conditions in the Ontonagon River. The fish were relocated to deeper water over multiple missions involving DNR technicians and community partners.

stories.title: DNR seeks $50M conservation easement in U.P. How you can tour property
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Natural Resources is working with Lyme Great Lakes Timberlands to create a 152,000-acre conservation easement in the Upper Peninsula, protecting forests, lakes, and wildlife habitats. The project, which could cost $50 million, includes public recreational access and is seeking remaining funding from state and federal sources. Public tours of the area are being offered before finalizing the deal.

stories.title: DNR seeks public input on management plans for Van Riper State Park and Michigan Iron Industry Museum property
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Natural Resources is seeking public input on new management plans for Van Riper State Park in Champion and the Michigan Iron Industry Museum property in Negaunee. Feedback via online surveys is open until November 1, 2026, to inform draft plans that will be shared with the public before approval.

stories.title: DNR shares photos of unique gray fox. Why it looks purple
stories.summary: The Michigan DNR shared photos of a rare melanistic gray fox that appears purplish in images, possibly the only one of its kind in the Midwest. The DNR clarified the fox is actually black, with the purple hue likely due to lighting or camera effects. The post also compared the fox's melanism to black squirrels in Michigan and confirmed the photos are not AI-generated.

photo.alt: Portrait of Dan Basso

stories.title: Do we lose or gain an hour in the fall?
stories.summary: Daylight Saving Time ends at 2 a.m. on Nov. 1, 2026, the first Sunday in November. Clocks will be set back one hour, leading to sunrise and sunset coming an hour earlier. While many digital devices automatically adjust, manual changes may be needed for analog clocks and some digital devices.

photo.alt: Do we lose or gain an hour in the fall?

stories.title: Do we set clocks back tonight? When DST ends in Michigan
stories.summary: Daylight Saving Time in Michigan ends at 2 a.m. on Nov. 1, 2026, with clocks falling back one hour. While many devices will adjust automatically, some clocks may need manual changes. The Sunshine Protection Act, which could make DST permanent, is unlikely to pass before this year's change.

photo.alt: Do we set clocks back tonight? When DST ends in Michigan

stories.title: Documents show DHS probed nonprofits, obtained millions of records in hunt for noncitizen voters
stories.summary: The Department of Homeland Security obtained tens of millions of unspecified records as part of a nationwide effort to investigate voter fraud, including potential undercover operations targeting nonprofit voter registration groups. Internal reports from May and June 2026 reveal Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) reviewed organizations in multiple states, with a focus on identifying noncitizen voting and groups suspected of illegal voter registration. The documents, obtained by Democracy Forward, highlight the Trump administration's push for election integrity ahead of the 2026 midterms.

stories.title: Domestic violence advocates urge passage of PPO bills
stories.summary: Domestic violence advocates in Michigan are urging lawmakers to eliminate fees for serving personal protection orders (PPOs), which could cost survivors hundreds of dollars. The state Senate and House have passed legislation to create a state fund covering these costs, but advocates fear time is running out before the end of the term. The issue gained urgency after a domestic violence survivor was killed following a delayed PPO service.

photo.alt: Domestic violence survivors and advocates Tanesha Ash-Shakoor, of Voices of Color, and Celeste Kanpurwala, of Moms Demand Action, embrace on the western steps of the Michigan Capitol on Thursday, September 14, 2023. Seventy empty pairs of shoes behind them represent the estimated 50 women and 20 children lost each year to firearm-related domestic violence.

The author emphasizes that getting involved can foster connections, personal growth, and a sense of belonging.

Stephanie Steen, who retired in March 2026, faces charges of making a false statement to U.S. agents after allegedly leaking details of a search warrant to her family in March 2025.

stories.title: Donald Trump vowed a ‘Michigan miracle.’ How that promise and others are going

While Trump has delivered on some pledges like tax breaks and immigration crackdowns, the 'Michigan miracle' of economic prosperity remains incomplete. Inflation and energy costs have risen, and the state's economy is in some ways worse than before Trump took office.

stories.title: DPSCD Continues Long-Term Improvement on 2026 M-STEP Results
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) showed noticeable improvements in all subjects and grades compared to 2019, with 7.6 percentage point growth in eighth-grade English proficiency and 6.8 percentage point growth in seventh-grade math. Despite a small dip in sixth-grade proficiency rates attributed to unfinished learning during the pandemic, the district's seventh-grade cohort outperformed peers, and SAT results also showed increases in English and math benchmarks.

stories.title: DPSCD’s board membership will change
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) board will undergo significant changes this year with five of seven seats up for election on Nov. 3. Only two incumbents are running, and current leaders LaTrice McClendon and Corletta Vaughn will not seek re-election. The board must also appoint a new member following the recent death of Iris Taylor before the election.

photo.alt: DPSCD’s board membership will change

stories.title: DPSCD’s new policy
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) has adopted a new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs, requiring documentation for early pickups and prohibiting them in the final 30 minutes of the school day. Parents will face mandatory meetings and attendance contracts if their children have multiple unexcused departures, with consequences including chronic absenteeism tracking and potential grade repetition.

stories.title: DPSCD’s results show continued growth
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) showed continued academic growth in 2026 M-STEP results, with significant improvements in English and math across multiple grades. While early literacy growth was smaller and sixth-grade proficiency dipped slightly, the district's seventh graders outperformed peers. SAT results also showed increases in English and math benchmarks compared to 2019.

photo.alt: DPSCD’s results show continued growth

stories.title: DPSCD teacher contract clears final hurdle to approval
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) teacher contract has been approved, including new guidelines on AI use in classrooms, lead teacher roles, and updated policies on maternity/paternity leave. While speech pathologist Michelle Awesome supports the leave policy, she criticizes the bonus system for exceeding caseload limits. The contract also adjusts transfer windows and professional development compensation rates.

stories.title: DPSCD teacher contract clears final hurdle to approval - Chalkbeat
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) has approved a new teacher contract with the Detroit Federation of Teachers, including provisions on AI usage in classrooms, lead teacher roles, and updated policies on maternity/paternity leave and professional development. The contract prohibits AI from replacing teacher judgment in grading or assessments and introduces a $3,000 annual stipend for lead teachers in core subjects. Additional changes include expanded leave protections and adjusted compensation for professional development workshops.

stories.title: DPSCD teacher contract clears final hurdle to approval
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) teacher contract has been approved, introducing new guidelines on AI use in classrooms, lead teacher roles with stipends, and updated professional development rates. The agreement includes provisions for AI tools to support instruction but prohibits their use in grading or discipline decisions. Other highlights involve a revised voluntary transfer window, sick day restoration for parents returning from leave, and allowances for religious observance absences. Speech pathologist Michelle Awesome praised some aspects but criticized the bonus system for exceeding caseload limits.

stories.title: DPSCD to roll out high school redesign focusing on career pathways for ninth graders
stories.summary: Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) will implement a high school redesign in fall 2026, with ninth graders at 11 neighborhood high schools exploring career pathways through a seminar class. The initiative includes smaller class sizes, additional tutoring for students behind in literacy, and hiring seven more counselors to achieve a 1:250 student ratio. Superintendent Nikolai Vitti emphasized reducing credit deficits to enable college and career course enrollment by 11th grade.

stories.title: DPSCD will add more initiatives to boost attendance
stories.summary: Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) will expand a yellow bus transportation pilot program to Pershing and Cody high schools and reintroduce a perfect attendance incentive for middle schoolers this school year. The district aims to reduce chronic absenteeism, which affected 60.9% of students in 2024-25, by implementing these initiatives.

stories.summary: The Draconids meteor shower is peaking on Oct. 8-9, offering ideal viewing conditions for casual skywatchers in Michigan. The shower begins soon after sunset with minimal moonlight interference, and favorable weather forecasts suggest clear skies for optimal viewing.

stories.summary: A 28-year-old man was arrested and charged with reckless driving causing serious impairment after a crash on the Mackinac Bridge injured four people and closed the bridge for several hours. stories.title: Drugs are widely used to sedate dementia patients. Her sons wanted to keep her off them.
stories.summary: Marjorie Tingley’s sons resisted requests to sedate their mother with antipsychotic medications at Vista Grande Villa, a Michigan senior living facility. The facility evicted her after repeated aggressive incidents, and she died less than two weeks later at a new facility. Her family’s lawsuit alleges negligence and retaliation, while Vista Grande claims the drugs were routine and the ER visits were due to the family’s refusal of on-site treatment.

stories.title: DTE appeals $100-million Zug Island judgment
stories.summary: DTE Energy has appealed a $100-million pollution fine ordered by U.S. District Judge Gershwin Drain, who mandated air pollution controls and community-funded air quality programs. The company seeks a stay to halt enforcement while appealing, arguing facility shutdown risks. Environmental groups and community advocates emphasize the need for continued engagement in shaping pollution mitigation efforts.

photo.alt: Environmental attorneys Nick Leonard, left, and Mary Rock represented the Sierra Club as intervenor plaintiffs in the Environmental Protection Agency’s Clean Air Act lawsuit against EES Coke Battery on Zug Island. stories.title: DTE Doubles Down on $1 Billion Investment to Modernize Detroit's Electric Grid
stories.summary: DTE Energy has invested over $1 billion in the past five years to modernize Detroit's electric grid, particularly on the east side and in the Islandview area. The company claims this investment helped restore power to 90% of customers within 48 hours after a recent storm and reduced outage durations by 91% from 2023 to 2025. DTE also reported trimming 350 miles of trees, upgrading 220 miles of infrastructure, and replacing 2,270 poles.

photo.alt: DTE Doubles Down on $1 Billion Investment to Modernize Detroit's Electric Grid

stories.title: DTE-funded group loses appeal to block Ann Arbor for Public Power ballot proposal
stories.summary: A2REC, a group backed by DTE Energy, lost its appeal to block a ballot proposal for a city-run power grid in Ann Arbor. The Michigan Court of Appeals upheld the city clerk's certification of signatures, rejecting claims that supplemental submissions violated state law. The proposal, which would allow voters to decide on transitioning to a publicly owned utility system, will remain on the 2026 midterm ballot.

photo.alt: People standing around booths at Liberty Plaza.

stories.title: DTE Gas seeks signals another rate hike request hours after $74.5-million jump
stories.summary: DTE is preparing another natural gas rate increase, filing notice just hours after Michigan regulators approved a $74.5-million hike that will raise typical residential bills by about $2.87 monthly. The amount of the new request, expected to be filed around Nov. 13, hasn’t been disclosed. Attorney General Dana Nessel criticized the timing as part of an 'unsustainable cycle' of rate cases. DTE says the notice is a required procedural step and won’t immediately affect bills, and said details on gas system investments are coming in November.

stories.title: Eastpointe police chase: Detroit man charged with fleeing police after alleged plant theft
stories.summary: A Detroit man accused of leading a police chase over stolen plants in Eastpointe is facing multiple felony charges, including second-degree fleeing and eluding police. The incident occurred early Friday morning when officers responded to a report of plant theft and attempted to arrest Jeremy Jamel Johnson, who fled in a truck with a trailer, causing an officer's leg to be run over. Johnson, who has a lengthy criminal history, was denied a lower bond and faces potential life imprisonment if convicted.

stories.title: Education will be a key topic as Benson and James face off in Michigan governor’s race
stories.summary: Michigan Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson and U.S. Representative John James won their respective primary elections and will compete in the Nov. 3 general election. Both candidates agree on addressing Michigan’s low literacy rates but differ on partisan issues like school choice and transgender student rights. Benson received over 80% of the Democratic vote while James secured 50% of the Republican vote.

stories.title: El presupuesto de este año no cubre una brecha histórica de financiamiento para estudiantes que aprenden inglés en Michigan - Chalkbeat
stories.summary: Detroit Public Schools Community District received $6.7 million in additional funds for over 7,400 English language learners during the 2025-26 school year, but did not receive funding for 1,041 students who scored 4.0 or higher on the WIDA assessment. Critics argue that multilingual intervention specialists hired with lawsuit funds cannot replace required English language development minutes, and performance gaps persist for ELL students. A senior student who transitioned to general education classes after scoring high on the WIDA assessment reported receiving no English instruction, highlighting systemic resource limitations.

La nueva ley establece un marco de financiamiento automático y requisitos de informes, aunque los fondos adicionales siguen siendo insuficientes para cubrir las necesidades de los estudiantes.

stories.title: El presupuesto de este año no cubre una brecha histórica de financiamiento para estudiantes que aprenden inglés en Michigan
stories.summary: El presupuesto estatal de 2026-27 para estudiantes que aprenden inglés en Michigan asciende a $75,3 millones tras un aumento de $12,5 millones, pero educadores y defensores lo califican como insuficiente para cubrir la histórica brecha de financiamiento. Aunque el aumento es visto como un paso positivo, críticos señalan que Michigan sigue entre los peores estados en financiamiento para estos estudiantes y que los fondos adicionales ($225 por estudiante anuales) son limitados. La nueva ley establece una fórmula ponderada automática de financiamiento y requisitos de informes, pero se reconoce que aún se necesita más inversión.

stories.title: El-Sayed, Rogers face voter opposition to data centers in crucial Senate race
stories.summary: Michigan's U.S. Senate race between Republican Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has become a focal point for voter concerns about data center development. Both candidates face scrutiny over their financial ties to tech companies and their positions on moratoriums for data centers, which 62% of likely voters oppose. The November 3 general election will determine a senator who could influence federal AI and data center policies affecting Michigan's utilities and environment.

stories.title: El-Sayed, Rogers trade barbs over Iran war, gas prices in Michigan Senate debate

While both supported temporarily suspending the federal gas tax, they disagreed on the war's economic impact and military effectiveness. Rogers accused El-Sayed of misleading voters, calling his campaign 'the best con I think I’ve ever seen,' while El-Sayed claimed Rogers changes positions to improve poll numbers.

stories.title: End inflation, lower interest, boost economy
stories.summary: Trump promised to end inflation and boost the economy through tax cuts and deregulation. While unemployment has slightly decreased, inflation remains at 3.4% (up from 3.0% when Trump took office) and mortgage rates remain high at 7%. Upper-income residents have benefited from stock market gains, but lower-income households have seen little improvement.

stories.summary: Trump promised to end inflation and boost Michigan's economy through tax cuts and deregulation. However, inflation remains at 3.4% as of August 2026, with food prices up 6-7% and mortgage rates at 7%. While the stock market has risen 22%, wage growth (3.6% in Michigan) lags behind national averages.

stories.title: Energy prices and policies

The US attacks on Iran and global events have disrupted energy markets despite record oil production.

stories.title: Energy prices and policy

The administration ended EV subsidies, saving $300 billion by 2035, but renewable energy still comprises 30% of US electricity. A $57 million loan aims to restart Michigan's Palisades nuclear plant.

Bragg's organs saved multiple lives, but her family advocates for banning e-bikes for children.

stories.summary: Attorneys representing the estate of John Jenuwine, a 34-year-old Navy veteran shot and killed by Washtenaw County sheriff deputies in January, have expanded their lawsuit against the county, adding six additional officers as defendants. The expanded filing follows a review of 250 gigabytes of newly obtained footage showing a different version of events than the initial narrative. The lawsuit alleges deputies withheld lifesaving aid and misrepresented Jenuwine's movements after he was shot.

stories.title: Family remembers Cehic as devoted husband
stories.summary: Cehic, a Bosnian immigrant, worked at a flea market to support his family. His wife, Sanela Grcic, described him as a kind and devoted husband, grieving his loss after her father's death two months prior. He leaves behind his wife, three adult children, and two teenagers.

stories.title: Family remembers woman killed in random downtown Detroit stabbing
stories.summary: Jaquoya Wix, a 34-year-old woman on break from her Chipotle job in downtown Detroit, was killed in a random stabbing on Sept. 20. Her family shared memories of her positive life changes and expressed grief over her death. Police captured the suspect via surveillance video and confirm the attack was random, with no charges filed yet. stories.title: 'Fast' meteor shower is set to start. When Orionids will peak
stories.summary: The Orionids meteor shower is set to begin this week and will peak in October, providing an extra bit of flare to the night sky around Halloween. The 'fast' meteor shower typically features 10 to 20 meteors per hour, streaking through the night sky at 41 miles per second, according to NASA. The shower is expected to peak overnight Oct. 21-22 and will be active until Nov. 7.

stories.summary: The FBI's Endangered Child Alert Program (ECAP) collaborates with the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children to identify child predators. Parents and schools are urged to monitor online activity to prevent exploitation.

stories.title: Federal appeals court vacates Trump order extending operations for a west Michigan coal plant
stories.summary: A federal appeals court has vacated an order from the Trump administration that extended the operations of the J.H. Campbell Coal Plant in Port Sheldon Township, Michigan. The court ruled that the U.S. Department of Energy exceeded its emergency authority under the Federal Power Act, emphasizing that states, not the federal government, should manage energy reliability planning. The plant, owned by Consumers Energy, was scheduled to close by 2025, with the court's decision aligning with state and regional grid operator approvals for its retirement.
