stories.title: Federal complaint alleges Medicaid fraud, forced labor by Quality Behavioral Health CEO
stories.summary: The federal government is seeking to seize nearly $19 million from Quality Behavioral Health, alleging its CEO used Medicaid beneficiaries as forced labor and submitted fraudulent claims. The civil forfeiture complaint, filed on September 22, 2026, follows an FBI search of the CEO's home and company locations in August. No criminal charges have been announced against the CEO.

stories.title: Federal Court Injunction Blocks Enforcement of Executive Order on Election Fraud
stories.summary: A federal court has issued an injunction preventing the implementation of Section 2 of an Executive Order related to election fraud, affecting 24 plaintiff states including Michigan. The order bars federal agencies from creating new programs to control state voter rolls or initiating investigations against state officials administering federal elections, except for providing requested assistance within congressional frameworks.

stories.title: Federal judge tosses Nessel suit accusing fossil fuel industry of anti-trust violations
stories.summary: A U.S. District Court judge dismissed Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel's lawsuit against major fossil fuel companies and an oil lobbying group, ruling she lacks standing to pursue federal antitrust claims. The case alleged the defendants conspired to limit renewable energy competition, but the judge found the state failed to prove proximate cause linking the conspiracy to higher energy costs. Nessel's office is reviewing the decision and considering next steps.

stories.summary: The U.S. Department of the Treasury released guidance for the federal Education Freedom Tax Credit program, allowing taxpayers to claim up to $1,700 in tax credits for donations to scholarship-granting organizations. The program, effective January 2026, has been adopted by 30 states, with rules requiring SGOs to allocate 90% of funds to scholarships and undergo annual audits. Democratic governors in some states have resisted participation while others plan to review federal guidelines before joining.

The lawsuit claims Ryan made unwelcome advances, created a hostile work environment, and was protected by the company’s HR department. Davis Cartage has not yet responded to the complaint.

stories.title: FEMA Imposes Election Administration Conditions on Homeland Security Grants
stories.summary: In June 2026, FEMA issued a Notice of Funding Opportunity requiring states to implement changes to election systems as a condition for Homeland Security Grant Program funds. Requirements include transitioning from electronic voting systems using bar codes/QR codes to hand-marked paper ballots, conducting 5% post-election manual audits, and reconciling voter counts with ballots cast. States must allocate at least 80% of funds to local and tribal governments.

stories.title: Festival of Oddities to move. Organizer says Charlotte is unwelcoming

The festival, held annually since 2019, plans to relocate to another Mid-Michigan community in 2027.

stories.title: Freaks and Geeks
stories.summary: Forever remembered as one of the great non-starters of ’90s television, creator Paul Feig and producer Judd Apatow’s sublime “Freaks and Geeks” now exists as one of the most effortlessly perfect things ever created. Set in a fictional Detroit suburb in the year 1980, the show stars Lindsay Weir (Linda Cardellini) and her younger brother Sam (John Francis Daley) as they navigate the awkwardness of high school. Lindsay hangs out with freaks and burnouts: there’s Nick (Jason Segel), the Rush-obsessed aspiring drummer, and Kim (Busy Philipps), the mean girl from a bad part of town. Meanwhile, Sam is an awkward geek who spends most of his time with fellow nerds Neal (Samm Levine) and Bill (Martin Starr). It’s hard to imagine why the show was ever cancelled: Every episode is a treasure trove of [pitch-perfect comedy](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dB_D_ZxGUWA) and [surprisingly tender moments](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cmCpmEQD0L4), featuring nearly every important comedy actor of the aughts and 2010s (no, [really](https://www.looper.com/820224/famous-actors-you-forgot-showed-up-on-freaks-and-geeks/)). Watch it now for an inviting fall atmosphere, a sneaky University of Michigan reference (“I mean, are the kids in Michigan schools that stupid?” might be the best line in the show) and one of the greatest finales in TV history.

stories.title: Gilmore Girls
stories.summary: There is no show as synonymous with fall as “Gilmore Girls.” Though the series concluded nearly two decades ago, fans annually rewatch all 153 episodes when summer ends. Following its resurgence with Generation Z, the Lorelais (mother-daughter co-protagonists who share the same name) returned for a renewal miniseries, “Gilmore Girls: A Year in the Life,” in 2016, but nothing holds up quite like the original. From Chilton Preparatory School to Yale University, follow Rory Gilmore’s (Alexis Bledel) journey through high school romance, friendship and rivalry, college applications and university life. While she’s funny, relatable and occasionally frustrating, the best part of Rory Gilmore is her heartwarming relationship with her mother, Lorelai (Lauren Graham), as she navigates growing up and finding independence. However, what truly keeps viewers coming back is the cozy, comforting atmosphere the show creates. Set in the small fictional town of Stars Hollow, Conn., the knit sweaters, pumpkin patches, cider mills and close-knit community perfectly embody the warmth of autumn. If you start the show today, you’ll watch the leaves turn and fall alongside the Gilmore girls, ready to do it all over again next year.

stories.title: Glacier Detachment in Nepal Triggers Floods in China and Nepal
stories.summary: A significant glacier detachment in Nepal on August 28, 2026, caused a flood that impacted downstream areas in both China and Nepal. The event, which mobilized material from a glacier at 5200 m a.s.l., met with previous flood deposits, leading to a dam failure and subsequent flooding. Satellite imagery and photos confirm the detachment and its effects.

stories.title: Grand Rapids community demands answers after Guatemalan man dies fleeing attempted ICE stop
stories.summary: A 35-year-old undocumented immigrant from Guatemala, Mario David Coronado Juárez, died after fleeing an ICE traffic stop and crashing into a tree in Grand Rapids on Sept. 20. Community members held a vigil on Sept. 24 demanding justice, while Rep. Hillary Scholten requested an investigation and ICE denied a car chase occurred. stories.title: Gubernatorial campaigns float gas tax suspensions as gas prices tick up across Michigan
stories.summary: Michigan gubernatorial candidates Jocelyn Benson (D) and John James (R) have both proposed suspending gas taxes to address rising fuel costs, though their approaches differ. James advocates suspending both federal and state gas taxes, while Benson previously called only for a federal tax suspension, warning that state-level cuts would harm road funding and budgets. The debate reflects broader concerns about affordability amid high gas prices linked to geopolitical tensions.

stories.title: Gun safety a necessary step in suicide prevention
stories.summary: Suicide deaths are the second leading cause of death for people aged 10-34 in Michigan, according to a report by the Michigan Suicide Prevention Council. Increased firearm access contributes to suicide, with states having higher gun ownership rates showing significantly higher suicide rates. Recommendations include securing firearms and limiting access for at-risk individuals, as well as sustaining state funding for suicide prevention infrastructure and aligning policies to educate professionals in risk assessment.

stories.title: High-risk pregnancy doctors publish new standards for care under state abortion bans

Research shows higher complication rates in restricted states, with 57% of cases experiencing severe issues compared to 33% in states without restrictions.

stories.summary: An Amish 16-year-old boy was killed in a farming accident on Sept. 28 when a horse-drawn wagon overturned in Sanilac County. The horse became spooked, causing the wagon to flip and trap the boy underneath. He was transported to a trauma center but later died.

stories.title: Horse from children’s book raises money for therapy
stories.summary: A miniature therapy horse named Fabio, who inspired Heather Bowman’s children’s book 'There’s a Horse in the House,' participated in a meet-and-greet event in South Lyon. The event, organized by Salem-South Lyon library and Tiny Treasures Therapy Horses, allowed families to interact with Fabio and purchase the book, with proceeds funding free horse therapy for those in need. The initiative also aims to boost children’s literacy in Michigan, where reading scores have declined significantly.

stories.title: Hot dorms at Michigan State University? How students are being told to stay cool

stories.title: House Bill 5081 Requires Schools to Employ Teachers Trained in Orton-Gillingham Approach for Dyslexia Support
stories.summary: House Bill 5081 mandates that school districts, intermediate school districts, and public school academies employ at least one teacher trained in the Orton-Gillingham approach to assist students with dyslexia. The bill requires annual professional development and estimates a one-time training cost of $1,500 per educator. It has no state fiscal impact but would cost local districts.

stories.title: House bill would give school credit for job experience
stories.summary: A bill passed in the Michigan House would grant academic credits to high school seniors working at least 30 hours per week in manufacturing, construction, or other fields with verifiable job training. The legislation aims to address skilled-trade worker shortages and provide alternative pathways to the American dream beyond college degrees. It now moves to the Democratic-controlled Senate after passing with limited bipartisan support.

stories.title: How 2027’s COLA could stack up
stories.summary: The predicted 2027 COLA would rank 19th among Social Security increases since 1977. The 2025 COLA tied for 27th, while the highest recorded COLA was 14.3% in 1980. Benefits cannot decrease by law, but no COLA is implemented if inflation is flat, as seen in 2010, 2011, and 2016.

stories.title: How does the sun's solar cycle impact winter?
stories.summary: High solar activity is linked to warmer temperatures, with Solar Cycle 25 peaking in 2024 and elevated sunspot activity potentially contributing to a warmer winter. The cycle began with a solar minimum in 2019 and is expected to end with the next solar minimum between 2029-2032.

stories.title: How hikers’ tip led to the rescue of nearly 30 lake sturgeon in the Upper Peninsula
stories.summary: Hikers on the North Country Trail reported three stranded lake sturgeon in the West Branch Ontonagon River, prompting the Michigan Department of Natural Resources to rescue nearly 30 fish. The sturgeon were relocated from a dewatered channel caused by hydroelectric operations at Victoria Dam. Lake sturgeon, listed as a threatened species since 1994, are long-lived and critical to the river's ecosystem.

stories.title: How much longer until DST ends for 2026?
stories.summary: Daylight Saving Time ends at 2 a.m. on Nov. 1, 2026, the first Sunday in November. Clocks will be set back one hour, leading to sunrise and sunset coming an hour earlier. While many digital devices automatically adjust, manual changes are needed for analog clocks and some digital devices.

stories.title: How strong will northern lights be over Michigan? See NOAA outlook

Mayor Christopher Taylor and four council members opposed the resolution, citing past community divisions and high costs, while supporters emphasized the need for data-driven research on deer overpopulation's ecological and safety impacts. stories.summary: Local authorities in Northern Michigan confirmed that immediate public health risks from a fiery F-16 fighter jet crash have ended. The crash occurred on Sept. 17, 2026, near Traverse City, leading to a one-mile evacuation and hospitalizations for some first responders due to hazardous chemical exposure. Health officials now state that drinking water remains safe and risks from explosion hazards and smoke inhalation are no longer concerns.

stories.title: Immigrant community reels after construction worker’s fatal crash fleeing ICE agents

His death has sparked outrage in the immigrant community, with advocates demanding justice and an independent investigation. Juarez, a married father of three, was working in the U.S. to build a home for his family in Guatemala.

stories.title: ‘Impossible to ignore’: Students call for divestment in walkout marking 3-year anniversary of Oct. 7 attacks
stories.summary: More than 100 students and activists participated in a walkout at the University of Michigan to mark three years since Hamas's Oct. 7, 2023 attack on Israel, demanding the university divest from financial and academic ties with Israel. The protest, organized by Students Allied for Freedom and Equality, included chants criticizing the university's response to pro-Palestine activism and Israel's military actions in Gaza, which have killed over 74,000 people and been classified as genocide by the UN. Speakers emphasized the power of student organizing and the need to end collaborations with a state 'actively participating in genocide.'

stories.title: Iron Mountain spruce chosen as Michigan Christmas tree. When it will be lit
stories.summary: A 60-foot spruce in Iron Mountain has been selected as the 2026 Michigan state Christmas tree, donated by the Larry Riccio family. The tree will arrive in downtown Lansing on Nov. 7 and be lit during the 42nd annual Silver Bells in the City celebration on Nov. 20. It will stand in front of the Capitol and is the second from Iron Mountain to be chosen for the capitol since 1987.

photo.alt: Iron Mountain spruce chosen as Michigan Christmas tree. When it will be lit

stories.title: IRS warning: Don’t fall for this, tax agency says in alert
stories.summary: The IRS has issued a warning about a scam offering fake 'Tribal Tax Credits' that do not exist under federal law. Scammers target taxpayers, tribal communities, businesses, and tax professionals, promising reduced tax liabilities or refunds. Claiming these fraudulent credits can result in civil and criminal penalties. The IRS emphasizes that no such government agreements with tribal groups exist and urges taxpayers to report suspicious offers.

photo.alt: IRS warning

stories.title: Is Daylight Saving Time ending this weekend?
stories.summary: Daylight Saving Time will end at 2 a.m. on Nov. 1, 2026, the first Sunday in November. Clocks will be set back one hour, leading to sunrise and sunset coming an hour earlier. While many digital devices automatically adjust, analog clocks and some digital devices may require manual changes.

photo.alt: Is Daylight Saving Time ending this weekend?

stories.title: Is fall here yet in Michigan?
stories.summary: The fall equinox occurs at 8:04 p.m. Sept. 22, marking the start of astronomical fall in Michigan. This event happens when the Earth tilts equally toward and away from the Sun, bringing nearly equal amounts of daylight to all latitudes.

photo.alt: Is fall here yet in Michigan?

stories.title: Is it too late to submit an item for the bucket list?
stories.summary: Submissions for the winter bucket list are open until noon on Monday, Oct. 20. The list seeks Michigan-based winter activities that involve more than just viewing, with a preference for those requiring winter gear and having an interesting backstory.

photo.alt: Bridge Lunch Break header image

stories.title: Is there a serial killer in Lansing? Here's what police say
stories.summary: Lansing police are investigating whether five deaths along the River Trail from October 2025 to August 2026 may be connected. The victims were men aged 22 to 70 with facial injuries or blunt-force trauma, and several died days after being found. Investigators face challenges due to few witnesses and limited surveillance, with only one case having an identified suspect.

source.name: Samantha Sayles, Amaya Kuznicki, Jeff Jewell

photo.alt: Is there a serial killer in Lansing? Here's what police say

stories.title: Isle Royale wolves inbred but likely to survive, study says
stories.summary: A study found that wolves reintroduced to Isle Royale National Park between 2018 and 2019 are inbred but have an over 80% chance of surviving for 20 years. Researchers tracked the population's development after 19 wolves were brought to the island to revive a dwindling population, noting challenges from inbreeding and climate-driven isolation. The wolf population has since grown to 37 individuals as of 2026, though inbreeding remains a concern.

photo.alt: A wolf relocated to Isle Royale between 2018 and 2019 leaves the crate it was transported in. (Courtesy of the National Park Service)

stories.title: Isle Royale wolves inbred but likely to survive, study says

stories.title: Issues of the Environment: How Washtenaw County is preparing for extreme weather before it hits
stories.summary: Washtenaw County is shifting from reactive disaster response to proactive planning through hazard mitigation plans. These plans identify vulnerabilities and prioritize infrastructure investments to reduce risks from flooding, extreme storms, and aging systems. Director Beth Gibbons emphasizes 'grounded hope'—pragmatic action to build resilience and access federal funding for pre-disaster preparedness.

photo.alt: Washtenaw County Resiliency Office Director Beth Gibbons.

stories.title: Issues of the Environment: U-M climate scientist gives safety tips during times of intensifying wildfires | WEMU-FM
stories.summary: Dr. Stuart Batterman from the University of Michigan discusses the health risks of wildfire smoke, including PM 2.5, ozone, and transported pathogens. He highlights vulnerable populations and affordable solutions like homemade air purifiers to mitigate exposure during smoke events.

photo.alt: Wildfire smoke plume with health warning signs

stories.title: IT Department student employee Bryan Utych receives Student Employee of Month award for September
stories.summary: Bryan Utych, an IT Department student employee, was recognized as the Student Employee of the Month for September. He frequently assists with password issues and other IT services at Schoolcraft College.

photo.alt: IT Department student employee, Bryan Utych (right) stands next to his supervisor, Jared Hynes, after receiving the Student Employee of Month award for September.

stories.title: 'It has broken my heart': Community members speak at U-M, Los Alamos data center town hall
stories.summary: Community members and University of Michigan officials gathered on Sept. 9, 2026, to discuss concerns about a $1.2 billion joint data center project between U-M and Los Alamos National Laboratory in Ypsilanti Township. Attendees voiced opposition to the facility's location near residential areas and the Huron River, while university officials emphasized mitigation measures like landscaped barriers. A follow-up town hall is scheduled for Oct. 1, 2026.

photo.alt: 'It has broken my heart': Community members speak at U-M, Los Alamos data center town hall

stories.title: It’s chipmunk season, Michigan. The cute critters are causing trouble once again
stories.summary: Michigan residents are experiencing property damage from chipmunks as the small animals burrow around homes and gardens, chew through wires, and disrupt landscaping. Experts from the Department of Natural Resources and Michigan Wildlife Conservancy advise addressing the root causes of chipmunk activity rather than relying on relocation, which requires a permit. Current regulations allow landowners to kill chipmunks causing damage without a permit, but relocation remains restricted to prevent spreading issues and disease.

photo.alt: A chipmunk digs in freshly disturbed soil beside a weathered wooden post.

stories.title: It's cider season in Michigan. Where to find fall's sweet treat
stories.summary: With the first official day of fall approaching, cider mills across Michigan are open for the season, offering family-friendly activities and opportunities to pick seasonal produce. The tradition, rooted in local agriculture, continues as Michigan's apple crop estimate for 2026 is reported to be below average. Cider mills from metro Detroit to Kalamazoo and beyond provide a sweet autumn experience for residents.

photo.alt: Portrait of Jalen Williams

stories.title: It's Debate Week in Michigan. Candidates for governor and US Senate face off.
stories.summary: As of Monday, October 5, more than 120,000 Michiganders have already voted. That's roughly 1.7% of active registered voters in Michigan.

photo.alt: A photo of people at voting booths is behind a light orange, gradient background. At the top is The Mids logo and underneath it are the words 'Election Security.'

stories.title: ‘It’s hard for me to let it go’: Another Jackson area restaurant announces closure
stories.summary: Ixcanul Guatemalan & Mexican Cuisine in Spring Arbor, MI, will close on Oct. 3, 2026, after struggling with economic challenges. Owner Mariano Caal expressed emotional difficulty in letting go of the restaurant, which opened during the pandemic and relied on community support. Factors like rising costs and shifting customer habits contributed to the decision.

photo.alt: Ixcanul Guatemalan & Mexican Cuisine owner Mariano Caal gets emotional as he talks about the closing of the restaurant on Tuesday morning, Sept. 29, 2026. The restaurant announced Monday that Saturday, Oct. 3 will be their last day of business.

stories.title: 'It’s really devastating': Westland parishioners rally to keep weekend masses
stories.summary: The Archdiocese of Detroit is considering changes that could end weekend Masses at parishes across Southeast Michigan. Westland parishioners at St. Mary, Cause of Our Joy, are concerned about losing weekend services and have started a petition with over 400 signatures. Westland Mayor Kevin Coleman also wrote a letter supporting the parish's request to remain fully open.

stories.summary: In 2026, Michiganders have already navigated severe spring storms, tornadoes and historic floods.

stories.title: It's World Space Week. See Michigan's ties to exploration
stories.summary: World Space Week, with the theme 'Rocket Revolution,' highlights Michigan's historical and modern connections to space exploration, including the Keweenaw Rocket Range and 34 astronauts with ties to the state. The event, held annually from Oct. 4-10, celebrates advancements in space launch technology and commercial access to space.

photo.alt: Image related to the article on World Space Week and Michigan's ties to space exploration

stories.title: Italian-inspired bar Aperitivo opens in downtown Ann Arbor
stories.summary: Aperitivo, a new wine and small plates bar inspired by Italian aperitivo culture, opened in downtown Ann Arbor in June. The bar offers a cozy ambiance, seasonal cocktails, and locally-sourced ingredients, catering to a 35+ crowd seeking a relaxed pre-dinner social space. Its design repurposes a historic building into an intimate lounge and open-air patio.

Bader won the Democratic primary with 56% of the vote, while Bearss secured the Republican nomination with 68%. Bierlein is running for Senate District 26 instead of seeking reelection. The district includes Frankenmuth, Vassar, Caro, and portions of Genesee County.

stories.title: Jackson factory evacuated for small fire
stories.summary: A Jackson factory was briefly evacuated on Sept. 22, 2026, after a small fire broke out at the CertainTeed Corporation facility on E Washington Ave. Fire crews evacuated 40-50 employees, extinguished the fire quickly, and found no injuries. The cause is under investigation but does not appear suspicious.

photo.alt: Jackson Fire Department responding to a factory fire. File photo.

stories.title: Jackson to showcase new Flatiron District housing development at open house
stories.summary: The City of Jackson and Norfolk Homes will host an open house on Oct. 8 to showcase homes under construction in the Flatiron District. The event replaces a previously canceled groundbreaking celebration and highlights the city's efforts to revitalize neighborhoods through new housing. City officials emphasized collaboration and infrastructure work in preparing the site for residential development.

photo.alt: Snow accumulates on the City of Jackson sign in Jackson on Saturday, Jan. 19, 2019.

stories.title: Jail partly evacuated during small fire in Monroe County
stories.summary: The Monroe County jail was partly evacuated on Sept. 21, 2026, after a small fire broke out in an unoccupied housing unit while contractors were working. No inmates were in the affected area, but a nearby occupied unit was evacuated as a precaution. The fire was quickly extinguished by jail staff and contractors, with assistance from the Monroe Department of Public Safety for smoke ventilation.

photo.alt: Police lights MLive

stories.summary: Jaycee Park's playground installation is nearly complete with ADA entrance ramps included. Pathway connections will be finalized through an upcoming project.

stories.title: “Jekyll & Hyde: The Musical,” Oct. 22–25
stories.summary: Ann Arbor Civic Theatre launches its mainstage season with Frank Wildhorn’s dramatic musical adaptation of Robert Louis Stevenson’s classic novel. The production follows Dr. Henry Jekyll’s dangerous experiment to separate the good and evil within humanity, resulting in the terrifying emergence of Edward Hyde. Featuring soaring music and gothic suspense, the production closes the month with one of musical theatre’s most enduring psychological thrillers.

photo.alt: “Jekyll & Hyde: The Musical,” Oct. 22–25

stories.title: Jewish and Democratic leaders urge El-Sayed to address Israel concerns
stories.summary: Jewish and Democratic Party leaders in Michigan have called on Abdul El-Sayed to address concerns about his criticism of Israel. Cantor Regina Hyatt expressed feeling alienated by political rhetoric, with many Jewish voters considering sitting out the election. El-Sayed has defended his stance on Israel while emphasizing his support for Jewish community safety.

photo.alt: Jewish and Democratic leaders urge El-Sayed to address Israel concerns

stories.title: Jewish groups mark 3-year anniversary of deadly Oct. 7 attacks
stories.summary: In the third anniversary of the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks in Israel, Oak Park's Jewish community center distributed memorial cards for each victim and held a remembrance event. The anniversary marks the first since the U.S. and Israel went to war with Iran. The attacks, coordinated by Hamas, killed 1,200 people and took 251 hostages.

photo.alt: Portrait of Frank Witsil

stories.title: Jocelyn Benson’s record: Election fights, faster DMV visits, transparency flop
stories.summary: Democratic Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson, running for governor, highlights her administrative efficiency and voting rights advocacy, including faster DMV services and expanded voting options. Critics argue she has politicized her office and faced transparency issues, while her tenure has included legal disputes over elections and voter roll management. Benson defends her record as data-driven and focused on saving Michiganders time and protecting voting rights.

stories.title: Journalist Peter Bergen talks implications of 9/11 attacks 25 years later
stories.summary: Twenty-five years after the 9/11 attacks, journalist Peter Bergen discussed their ongoing implications and legacy. Bergen, known for his expertise on terrorism, analyzed how the attacks reshaped global security and U.S. foreign policy.

stories.title: Just 1 in 4 Michigan juniors are ‘college ready,’ SAT scores indicate
stories.summary: Only 25.3% of Michigan high school juniors are considered college ready based on SAT scores, marking a decline from previous years. The College Board defines college readiness as a 75% chance of earning at least a C in first-semester college courses. School leaders emphasize that metrics like Advanced Placement courses and career tech programs also reflect readiness.

photo.alt: A student takes a practice exam to prepare for the SAT. Statewide, 26.5% of students met the ‘college ready’ math benchmark during the 2025-2026 school year and 52.1% met the reading and writing mark. (AP Photo/Butch Dill)

stories.title: Justin Trudeau says Trump’s ‘win-lose’ approach is hurting U.S.-Canada relations at Brown lecture
stories.summary: Former Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau criticized former U.S. President Donald Trump's 'win-lose' approach to trade, arguing it has strained U.S.-Canada relations and harmed American consumers through tariffs on aluminum and lumber. Speaking at Brown University's Ogden Memorial Lecture, Trudeau contrasted Canada's 'mosaic' approach to diversity with the U.S. 'melting pot' and defended Canada's universal healthcare system against American criticisms. The event highlighted ongoing tensions between the two nations over trade policies and differing governance models.

photo.alt: Brown University President Christina Paxson asks a question of the Rt. Hon. Justin Trudeau, Canada’s 23rd prime minister during the Ogden Memorial Lecture on International Affairs in the Pizzitola Sports Center on Tuesday, Sept. 22, 2026. (Photo by Nick Dentamaro/Brown University)

stories.title: K-12 spending, absenteeism programs face risks as feds stop key monitoring, watchdog says
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Education's suspension of a comprehensive monitoring process has increased the risk of undetected waste, fraud, and abuse in K-12 funding, according to a Government Accountability Office report. The report also highlighted unreliable absenteeism data, with some schools reporting rates over 100%, and noted the lack of a timeline for resuming federal compliance reviews.

stories.title: K-2 reading growth slowed last year in the Detroit district. Here’s what administrators say caused it.
stories.summary: Reading growth for Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) students in kindergarten to second grade stalled in the 2025-26 school year, despite initial improvements from a $94.4 million literacy lawsuit settlement. Superintendent Nikolai Vitti attributed the slowdown to insufficient individualized interventions for students near grade level and challenges like undiagnosed disabilities, chronic absenteeism, and summer learning loss. The district’s results showed 27.3% of K-2 students were proficient in reading, up less than 1 percentage point from the previous year.

stories.title: Kalamazoo boil water advisory could lift Monday after clean test results

The city expects to end the advisory Monday, Sept. 21, if additional samples analyzed Monday morning also come back clean. Public Services staff are collecting those samples over the next 24 hours while crews continue flushing the water system and conducting additional checks.

Trust and credibility with at-risk individuals and communities were critical to success, supported by the city’s financial backing and operational autonomy.

stories.title: Los Angeles Charter Amendment EE on Ethics, Elections, and Governance
stories.summary: Los Angeles voters will decide on a charter amendment to strengthen ethics and governance reforms, including increasing penalties for campaign finance violations, requiring weekly City Council meetings, and enhancing the independence of oversight bodies. The proposal also limits post-office political activity for Ethics Commission members and raises signature requirements for referendums.

stories.title: Los Angeles Charter Amendment Proposes Doubling Recreation and Parks Budget Over Ten Years
stories.summary: A proposed amendment to the City of Los Angeles Charter seeks to increase the minimum General Fund budget allocation for the Department of Recreation and Parks from 0.0325% to 0.065% of assessed property value over ten years. This phased increase aims to address service reductions and park equity gaps without creating new taxes, with exceptions allowing temporary reductions during fiscal emergencies. A 'yes' vote supports the increase, while a 'no' vote opposes it.

stories.title: Los Angeles Voters to Decide on 0.5% Sales Tax for Fire Department Funding in November 2026
stories.summary: Los Angeles voters will decide in November 2026 whether to approve a 0.5% sales tax to fund the Los Angeles Fire Department. The tax would generate approximately $345 million annually for staffing, equipment, fire stations, and wildfire preparedness, with annual audits and a Citizens’ Oversight Committee. The measure requires maintaining minimum General Fund spending for the department based on historical levels.

stories.title: Los Angeles Voters to Decide on Charter Amendments for Infrastructure, Budget, and Contracting
stories.summary: Los Angeles voters will decide on a charter amendment proposing changes to infrastructure planning, budget cycles, public works governance, and contracting rules. The measure would establish a two-year budget cycle, expand the Director of Public Works' authority, remove restrictions on city commercial activities and property mortgages, and adjust competitive bidding requirements for contracts. A 'yes' vote supports these reforms, while a 'no' vote opposes them.

stories.title: Macomb County eyes $6.79M cloud platform for emergency records, dispatch
stories.summary: Macomb County will migrate its emergency dispatch and records management systems to a cloud-based platform under a $6.79 million contract with Tyler Technologies. The Records and Public Safety Committee approved the five-year agreement on Sept. 17, 2026, which consolidates public safety technology across municipal boundaries and aims to enhance data sharing between agencies. The Sheriff’s Office will pay $2.1 million over five years, with affiliated agencies covering the remaining $4.7 million.

She is charged with five felonies and one misdemeanor, with a $250,000 bond.

The roundabout aims to address traffic congestion and reduce angle crashes at the intersection.

stories.title: Making Movies
stories.summary: Making Movies is the Latin Grammy–nominated group led by Enrique Chi, born in Santiago, Panamá, and raised in the American Midwest. The band blends rumbero percussion, delicate organs, and grungy fuzz, with NPR calling them 'one of the most unique groups around today.' Their sound incorporates the traditional Panamanian instrument, the mejorana.

stories.title: Man accused of killing woman in random attack in downtown Detroit denied bond
stories.summary: Devon Jason Watson was charged with first-degree murder for stabbing Jaquoya Wix, 34, to death in a random attack in downtown Detroit on Sept. 20. He faces charges including larceny over $20,000 and unlawful driving of an automobile.

stories.title: Man arrested after police seize hundreds of pills, multiple weapons from Shelby Township home

Detectives from the Macomb County Sheriff’s Office and Warren Police Department executed the warrant on Sept. 17, recovering firearms, ammunition, drug paraphernalia, and $16,000 in cash. Cholagh faces felony charges related to drug distribution and firearm offenses.

photo.alt: Mark Cholagh, 45, of Macomb Township, is facing multiple charges after a police search warrant in Shelby Township uncovered multiple guns, hundreds of pills, drug paraphernalia, packaging materials and cash.

Donevan Brueggeman, 27, of Cedarville, faces charges of operating under the influence causing incapacitating injury and a moving violation causing serious impairment of body function. He was arraigned on September 29, 2026, with a $10,000 bond.

stories.summary: Sterling Anthony Peters, 55, of Detroit, has been charged with one count of false report or threat of terrorism after allegedly threatening Detroit Mayor Mary Sheffield and attempting to enter city buildings. Officials say Peters threatened to shoot up the Coleman A. Young Municipal Center on Oct. 5 and later threatened physical harm to Sheffield at Detroit Public Safety Headquarters. stories.title: Man dead after fleeing ICE agents in Grand Rapids

The crash occurred near Century Avenue and McKendrick Street, with the driver pronounced dead at the scene. ICE agents attempted to stop him before the crash, and the Grand Rapids Police Department has referred the investigation to Michigan State Police due to the case's complexity. U.S. Rep. Hillary Scholten has demanded transparency and accountability from ICE regarding the incident.

stories.title: Michigan Agencies to Post Grant Reports by March 15 and Update by June 15 and September 15
stories.summary: Michigan state agencies must post grant reports by March 15 of the fiscal year and update them by June 15 and September 15. The reports must include comprehensive information about grants awarded, as mandated by the Management and Budget Act.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $1.3 Million for Stormwater Management in Ox Creek Watershed
stories.summary: The state has allocated $1.3 million for a stormwater management project in the Ox Creek Watershed. The project will be executed by state employees or contracted service providers and is expected to be completed by September 30, 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $1.595 Billion for Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity in FY2027 Budget
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity will receive $1.595 billion in funding for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, including $355.5 million from the state general fund and over $1 billion in federal revenues.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $1.5M for Pediatric Dentistry Clinic
stories.summary: The Department of Health will allocate $1.5 million to Team Cares to support a pediatric and sedation dentistry clinic. The project, funded through work project funds, will be completed by September 30, 2030, and is managed by a CARF International accredited wellness center.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $1 Million for Future Mobility and Electrification Projects
stories.summary: The state of Michigan has allocated $1 million to support the emerging aviation and advanced air mobility sector through the Office of Future Mobility and Electrification. Funds will be used for infrastructure deployment, industry development, and workforce strategies. The project is expected to be completed by September 30, 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $1 Million for Literacy Program Implementation
stories.summary: The state appropriates at least $1 million for implementation costs of literacy programs funded under the state school aid act.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $125,000 for Renewable Energy and Electrification Infrastructure Grants
stories.summary: The Michigan Public Service Commission will review and award grants for renewable energy and electrification infrastructure projects, prioritizing distressed areas defined by blight designations, high poverty/unemployment rates, or environmental burdens. Recipients must submit post-project reports and administrative costs are capped at $125,000. RNG is defined as methane from organic waste sources.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $13.9 Million for Higher Education and Student Support in 2026-2027 Budget
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget for fiscal year 2026-2027 includes $13.9 million in appropriations for the Office of Higher Education, covering dual enrollment payments, student financial assistance programs, and classified positions. An additional $4 million in one-time funding supports college success initiatives, wraparound student services, and adult education programs. Funds are sourced from the state general fund, merit award trust fund, and other restricted revenues.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $150,000 for School Board Member Training
stories.summary: The state allocates $150,000 for school board member training programs covering topics like conflicts of interest, labor relations, education law, and governance.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $150M for Educator Compensation in 2026-2027
stories.summary: The Michigan legislature allocates $150 million for 2026-2027 to increase educator compensation in districts and intermediate districts. Funds must be used for educator pay raises, with collective bargaining required if unions are present. Payments are defined as 1-time bonuses not counted toward retirement contributions.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $174M for Pension Legacy Costs in FY27 Budget
stories.summary: The FY27 General Omnibus Bill (SB 878/PA 21 of 2026) authorizes $174.4 million in pension-related legacy costs for Michigan state departments through September 30, 2027. The budget includes administrative requirements for fund expenditure, reporting obligations for work project accounts, and policies prioritizing American and Michigan-made goods and services. Additional provisions address workforce management, space utilization assessments, and support for geographically disadvantaged businesses.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $18 Million for Workforce Development Projects
stories.summary: The state has designated $18 million for workforce development to meet federal work requirements under Public Law 119-21. Unexpended funds will remain available until projects are completed, with a tentative completion date of September 30, 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $190,000 for Educator Recruitment and Preparation Programs
stories.summary: The state budget allocates at least $190,000 and 1.0 FTE position for educator recruitment and preparation programs from funds appropriated in part 1.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $1M for Group-Based Prenatal Care Programs
stories.summary: The state will allocate $1 million to support prenatal healthcare providers offering group-based prenatal care programs. These programs involve small groups of expectant mothers in the same pregnancy phase receiving health services and discussions.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $2.75M for Rural Home Visit Program
stories.summary: The state will allocate at least $2.75 million from the general fund to support a rural home visit program for prenatal care. The Department of Health and Human Services must give equal consideration to all eligible evidence-based providers across regions when contracting for these services.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $2.9M for Northwest Michigan Dental Clinic Expansion
stories.summary: The Department of Health will allocate $2.9 million to Northwest Michigan Health Services, Inc., to open a larger, more comprehensive dental clinic supporting United We Smile. The project aims to improve dental care access in the region.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $2 Million for SMART Manufacturing Grant Program
stories.summary: The state has allocated $2 million for a SMART manufacturing grant program. The project will be executed by state employees or contracted service providers and is expected to be completed by September 30, 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $2 Million for Tribal Government Grants
stories.summary: Michigan has appropriated $2 million for tribal government grants to fund essential services for federally recognized tribal governments. Funds will be distributed according to an allocation plan recommended by the Inter-Tribal Council of Michigan.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $200K for Volunteer Dental Program for the Uninsured
stories.summary: A competitive grant of $200,000 will be allocated to administer a volunteer dental program providing services to uninsured individuals. The funding comes from dental program appropriations.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $20M for Community Navigation Partners
stories.summary: The state will allocate up to $20 million to community navigation partners to assist Michiganders in maintaining healthcare access during Medicaid and SNAP eligibility changes. The program prioritizes MI Bridges Community Partners and provides outreach and support through nonprofit agencies.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $23.5M for Direct Care Wage Increase in 2027
stories.summary: The state has allocated $23.5 million to continue direct care wage increases effective January 1, 2027, under the Improved Workforce Opportunity Wage Act. Funds will support minimum hourly wage rate increases.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $250,000 for AI Model Policies and Integration
stories.summary: A one-time appropriation of $250,000 will fund the development of state AI policies and tools for education. The funds will support integrating artificial intelligence into teaching, learning, and assessment services for school districts.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $250,000 to Veterans' Apprenticeship Programs in Construction Industry
stories.summary: The state of Michigan has allocated $250,000 to recruit and assist veterans in transitioning into apprenticeship programs within the construction industry. These funds may be contracted to a national nonprofit program that connects military service members with skilled training opportunities.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $299,700 for Maternal Health Policy Implementation
stories.summary: The state will allocate $299,700 to implement 2024 PA 256, which covers maternal health policy changes under Michigan Compiled Law 395.361 to 395.369. This funding supports legislative mandates for maternal health improvements.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $310 Million for School Safety and Mental Health in 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 Budgets
stories.summary: Michigan has allocated $300 million from the state school aid fund and $21 million from the general fund for the 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 fiscal years to support school safety and mental health initiatives. Funds may be used to hire or contract support staff for student mental health needs, including school psychologists, and to provide payments to districts, intermediate districts, nonpublic schools, and the Michigan Schools for the Deaf and Blind that opt in. The estimated completion date of the work project is December 31, 2026.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $4.26M for Dental Oral Assessment Program
stories.summary: The state will allocate $4.26 million, plus private contributions, to establish and maintain a dental oral assessment program. A report summarizing dental reports from schools must be submitted by December 31 of the current fiscal year.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $4.406 Million for Heavy-Duty Vehicles Program
stories.summary: The state has allocated $4.406 million for a heavy-duty vehicles program. The project will be executed by state employees or contracted service providers and is expected to be completed by September 30, 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $4M for Home Help Caregiver Council
stories.summary: Funds are designated to support the Home Help Caregiver Council and related activities under the 2024 PA 144 act, with an estimated cost of $4,000,000.00 by September 30, 2031.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $4M for Prenatal Care Outreach
stories.summary: The state will allocate $4,000,000.00 for prenatal care outreach and service delivery support, following the same allocation method as described in section 1348 of the budget act.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $5.6M for Robotics Education Grants in 2025-2026 Budget
stories.summary: Michigan's legislature has allocated $5.6 million for competitive grants to support robotics education programs in public and nonpublic schools. Funds will support pre-K to 12th grade students through partnerships with providers like FIRST Robotics and VEX. Payments must be made by December 1, 2026, with continued funding intended through 2027-2028.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $5M for Local Collaboratives to Improve Maternal and Infant Health
stories.summary: The state will allocate $5 million to support grants for local collaboratives that coordinate maternal and infant health outcomes. Recipients must be part of a perinatal quality collaborative.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $5M for Mobile Health Alliance Community Screenings
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Health will allocate $5 million to Mobile Health Alliance for community health screenings and data collection on underserved populations, first responders, and veterans. The project, funded through work project funds, aims to reduce health disparities in rural and medically underserved communities by 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $6.5 Million for Detroit and Rouge River Restoration
stories.summary: The state has allocated $6.5 million for restoration work in the Detroit and Rouge River areas of concern. The project will be executed by state employees or contracted service providers and is expected to be completed by September 30, 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $685,000 for High-Emission Vehicle Replacement
stories.summary: The state has allocated $685,000 to replace high-emission vehicles. The project will be executed by state employees or contracted service providers and is expected to be completed by September 30, 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $700,000 for Food Waste Reduction Initiative
stories.summary: The state has allocated $700,000 to support food waste reduction efforts. The project will be executed by state employees or contracted service providers and is expected to be completed by September 30, 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates Funds for Early Childhood Education and Literacy Programs
stories.summary: The Michigan Legislature has allocated funds for early childhood education and literacy programs, aiming to increase workforce numbers, enhance professional development, and support literacy coaches in intermediate districts. The initiatives include stipends, grants, and partnerships with public universities, with a completion date set for September 30, 2029.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates Funds for Educator Development and Grow Your Own Programs
stories.summary: Michigan has allocated $70 million for 2025-2026 and $25 million for 2026-2027 to support educator development and 'grow your own' programs through competitive grants. Funds will be distributed to districts, intermediate districts, and consortia for teacher recruitment, retention, and training, with requirements for cost-free participation and partnerships with accredited educator preparation programs. Programs must address critical education workforce needs and demonstrate measurable outcomes.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates Funds for Special Education Programs in 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 Fiscal Years
stories.summary: Michigan's legislature has allocated state and federal funds for special education programs in the 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 fiscal years, including reimbursements for districts and intermediate districts. The document outlines specific funding amounts, a weighted funding formula intent for 2028, and provisions for remote learning research and assessment tools development.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates Rural Jobs and Capital Investment Funds
stories.summary: Funds from the rural jobs and capital investment appropriation will be used to provide grants, loans, or other economic assistance to rural areas in Michigan through the MEDC and state departments. Unexpended funds will remain available until projects are completed.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates Supplemental Funding for 2026 with Contingency Authorizations and Legacy Cost Provisions
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget for fiscal year 2027 includes $26.4 million in contingency authorizations across federal, state, local, and private sectors, along with $21.5 million in pension-related legacy costs. The document outlines reporting requirements for work project funds, in-person workforce utilization, and restrictions on foreign goods procurement. Funds are subject to transfer rules under the Management and Budget Act.

stories.title: Michigan Allows ARPA Fund Reallocation for Public Health and Safety Employee Payroll
stories.summary: The state budget director may reallocate ARPA funds to reclassify general fund appropriations for payroll and benefits of eligible public health and safety employees at the Department of Corrections and State Police. Reallocation must comply with ARPA guidance and notify legislative committees within 10 business days.

stories.title: Michigan Allows Carryover of Unexpended Teacher Testing Fees
stories.summary: Revenue from unexpended teacher testing fees at the end of the fiscal year may be carried over to the next year and will not revert to the general fund.

stories.title: Michigan and 21 other states win suit against Trump's USDA
stories.summary: Michigan and 21 other states won a federal court case against the Trump administration's USDA, blocking guidelines that restricted SNAP eligibility for non-citizens. The court ruled the USDA's retroactive adjustment period was invalid, preventing potential financial penalties for states. The decision does not reverse eligibility restrictions from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

photo.alt: Michigan residents receiving SNAP benefits

stories.title: Michigan and New Mexico States Under Legal Review for Compliance with Court Order
stories.summary: Michigan and New Mexico are undergoing legal review to ensure compliance with the federal court's injunction in State of California v. Trump (No. 26-J1581). This follows a directive from the court to prevent enforcement of specific provisions of the Executive Order related to election administration.

stories.title: Michigan Announces Fiscal Year 2026 Supplemental Budget Allocations
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget for fiscal year 2025-2026 allocates $45 million in total state spending, with $27.97 million directed to local units of government through acquisition and development grants-in-aid. The document also details lapsing funds for specific natural resources trust projects, including $300,000 for Sycamore Creek Land Acquisition and $1.2 million for Rogue River State Game Area Land Acquisition, which will be reallocated to the Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund. Additional provisions include perpetual public recreation land use requirements and mineral royalty agreements for parcels over 5 acres.

stories.title: Michigan Appropriates $2.6 Billion for Higher Education in 2027 Fiscal Year
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, allocates $2.6 billion for higher education. Funding includes federal revenues, state general funds, and other restricted sources, with specific appropriations detailed for public universities like Central Michigan University, Eastern Michigan University, and others. Community colleges must meet performance funding criteria, including participation in the Michigan Transfer Network.

stories.title: Michigan Appropriates Funds for Department of Lifelong Education, Advancement, and Potential
stories.summary: The Department of Lifelong Education, Advancement, and Potential receives line-item appropriations for fiscal year 2026-2027, including 6.0 full-time unclassified positions.

stories.title: Michigan Appropriates Over $8.1 Billion for State Transportation Department in FY2026-2027 Budget
stories.summary: The Michigan state transportation department has been allocated over $8.1 billion for the fiscal year 2026-2027, including interdepartmental grants, federal revenues, and other restricted funds. The budget outlines gross appropriation, adjusted gross appropriation, and various revenue sources. The funds are intended for transportation-related projects and services, with no direct allocation from the state general fund.

stories.title: Michigan Attorney General's Legal Reimbursements and Reporting Requirements
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Attorney General must submit a report by March 1 detailing reimbursements received under the State Correctional Facility Reimbursement Act, including expenditure descriptions, investigation costs, and general fund credits. This provision outlines specific reporting obligations for legal reimbursements related to the Michigan Department of Corrections.

stories.title: Michigan backs legal challenge to scrapped carbon standards for power plants
stories.summary: A coalition of 25 states and cities, including Michigan, sued the Trump administration’s EPA to overturn its rollback of 2024 power plant carbon limits. Michigan’s AG Dana Nessel warned of worsened extreme weather. The coalition argues the EPA ignored alternatives and health/climate costs and will also challenge weakened fuel economy standards.

photo.alt: Avatar photo

stories.title: Michigan backs legal challenge to scrapped carbon standards for power plants
stories.summary: A coalition of 25 states and cities, including Michigan, sued the Trump administration’s EPA to overturn its rollback of 2024 limits on power plant greenhouse gas emissions. Michigan’s AG Dana Nessel warned that added pollution would worsen extreme weather. The coalition argues the EPA ignored alternatives and health/climate costs.

photo.alt: Michigan backs legal challenge to scrapped carbon standards for power plants

stories.title: Michigan Bill Allocates $2.3 Billion for Higher Education in 2026-2027 Fiscal Year
stories.summary: A Michigan legislative bill (HCB 5630) appropriates $2.3 billion for higher education in the 2026-2027 fiscal year, with conditions requiring community colleges to participate in the Michigan Transfer Network and submit course equivalency updates. Performance funding payments are contingent on compliance with these requirements.

stories.title: Michigan Bill Allocates $3M for Literacy Programs via Public Universities
stories.summary: A Michigan legislative bill proposes allocating up to $3 million to a public university partnered with a statewide educational media service. The funds must expand literacy programming, educator resources, and family engagement, with requirements for free standards-aligned content delivery through broadcast and digital platforms. The implementation deadline is February 1, 2028.

stories.title: Michigan Bill Outlines Funding for Teacher Education and Student Support Services
stories.summary: The bill allows approved teacher education institutions to use student support services funding in coordination with Morris Hood, Jr. funding. Institutions must report unobligated funds by April 15, 2026, with unspent funds reallocated to other institutions. The state budget director is required to expend all fiscal recovery funds by December 31, 2026.

stories.title: Michigan bill would shift election duties if the secretary of state also runs for office
stories.summary: A proposed Michigan bill (House Bill 5968) would require the deputy secretary of state to assume election oversight duties when the secretary of state is running for any office other than reelection. The legislation, backed by House Republicans, aims to formalize voluntary recusal policies like those implemented by Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson, who is currently the Democratic gubernatorial nominee. The bill would not apply to election audits or constitutional requirements, and critics argue it targets specific individuals rather than addressing broader election administration issues.

photo.alt: Michigan bill would shift election duties if the secretary of state also runs for office

stories.title: Michigan bills aimed at improving student literacy clear House committee
stories.summary: A Michigan House committee approved several bills Wednesday aimed at improving literacy in schools, including one requiring specialized training for all K-5 teachers. The legislation now moves to the full House for consideration. Literacy has been a top priority in the state legislature after poor reading scores on national and state exams.

photo.alt: Michigan bills aimed at improving student literacy clear House committee

stories.title: Michigan bird migration season is flying by. Here’s where to see the birds and how to protect them
stories.summary: Thousands of birds migrate through Michigan in late September and early October, with over 380 species passing through. Birdwatchers can spot warblers and other species at locations like the Nichols Arboretum, but birds face hazards like building collisions and climate change impacts.

photo.alt: An illustration of birds migrating at night with a glowing cityscape in the background.

stories.title: Michigan bottle refund rate falls to 69.4% as retailers push to overhaul bottle bill
stories.summary: Michigan’s 50-year-old bottle deposit system faces renewed scrutiny after the state’s refund rate dropped to 69.4% in 2025, its lowest level in decades. Independent grocers argue the system is costly and creates health and safety concerns, while shoppers highlight the 10-cent deposit as a key recycling incentive.

photo.alt: Michigan bottle refund rate falls to 69.4% as retailers push to overhaul bottle bill

stories.title: Michigan bottle return rate falls to 69.4% as retailers push to overhaul bottle bill
stories.summary: The Midwest Independent Retailers Association surveyed Michigan stores, finding over 90% want bottles and cans removed from grocery stores due to health, safety, and labor concerns. Retailers argue the process is time-consuming, dirty, and offers no financial benefit, prompting calls to reform the bottle bill system.

photo.alt: Image related to the bottle return issue

stories.title: Michigan Budget Allocates Funds for Interstate Licensure Compact Implementation
stories.summary: Funds for compact implementation fees will cover dues, IT systems, and costs for interstate licensure compacts the state joins or is already a member of.

stories.summary: The Michigan Chamber of Commerce endorsed Republican John James for governor of Michigan in the Nov. 3 general election.

stories.title: Michigan corrections officer accused of exposing himself to colleague ‘on multiple occasions’
stories.summary: A 36-year-old corrections officer at the Gus Harrison Correctional Facility in Adrian, Michigan, faces criminal sexual conduct charges after allegedly exposing himself to a colleague on multiple occasions between 2024 and 2025. Jonathan Sipes was arraigned on charges including third-degree and fourth-degree criminal sexual conduct, as well as aggravated indecent exposure. The incidents allegedly occurred at the facility and in its parking lot, with the case investigated by Michigan State Police. Sipes is scheduled for a preliminary exam on October 14, 2026.

photo.alt: Michigan corrections officer accused of exposing himself to colleague ‘on multiple occasions’

stories.title: Michigan country artist Waylon Hanel wins Artist of the Year at Nashville awards show
stories.summary: Waylon Hanel, a self-taught traditional country singer-songwriter from Millington, Michigan, won the Artist of the Year – Traditional/Classic Country award at the 2026 Josie Music Awards on Sunday, Sept. 20, at the Grand Ole Opry House in Nashville.

photo.alt: Michigan country artist Waylon Hanel wins Artist of the Year at Nashville awards show

stories.title: Michigan Court of Appeals directed to review convicted school shooter Ethan Crumbley's appeal of life without parole sentence
stories.summary: A Michigan court has directed a review of Ethan Crumbley's life without parole sentence for the 2021 Oxford High School shooting. The case involves determining if the teen should be eligible for parole after serving his sentence.

photo.alt: Oakland County Prosecutor Karen McDonald proceeds with an opening statement as defendant Ethan Crumbley listens in Pontiac, Michigan.

stories.title: Michigan dam safety overhaul advances after years of failed attempts
stories.summary: Lawmakers are advancing a sweeping rewrite of Michigan’s dam safety law, six years after a catastrophic failure exposed weaknesses in how aging dams are regulated. The Michigan House voted 96-7 on Sept. 22, 2026, to approve Senate Bill 947, which would require more frequent inspections of high-risk dams, establish a new registration system for dam owners, and mandate long-term maintenance planning. The bipartisan effort follows the 2020 Edenville and Sanford dam failures, which caused $175 million in property damage and forced thousands to evacuate.

photo.alt: LaBarge Dam on the Thornapple River near Caledonia, Mich., March 20, 2026. Federal regulators rated the high-hazard dam in poor condition following a September 2025 inspection.

stories.title: Michigan data-center tax incentives secret
stories.summary: Revisits the 2024 expansion of Michigan’s sales and use tax exemption for data centers, highlighting that the law prevents the Michigan Economic Development Corporation from disclosing information about applicants.

photo.alt: Michigan Data Center Report

stories.title: Michigan Department to Establish Precontract Risk Assessment Policy
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services must establish a policy for conducting precontract risk assessments to evaluate contractor financial risk, security risks, and insurance requirements. A report on assessments and contracts executed under the policy is due by March 31, 2027.

stories.title: Michigan Departments Required to Report Federal Policy Impacts
stories.summary: By December 31 and June 1, Michigan departments must report federal guidelines, rules, or policy changes that significantly impact their operations, including changes in federal revenue and public health or welfare implications.

stories.title: Michigan Designates $10M for Nursing Home Staffing Initiative
stories.summary: Unexpended funds for nursing facility staffing are designated as work project appropriations, aiming to address chronic workforce shortages with an estimated completion cost of $10,000,000.00 by September 30, 2031.

stories.title: Michigan districts say they don’t receive enough funding for English learners. Here’s what’s at stake.
stories.summary: Michigan districts report insufficient funding for English learners, highlighting ongoing challenges in supporting this student population.

photo.alt: Michigan districts say they don’t receive enough funding for English learners. Here’s what’s at stake.

stories.title: Michigan districts say they don’t receive enough funds for English learners
stories.summary: Districts in Michigan report insufficient funding for students learning English, particularly those with higher English proficiency. There are no specific funds for students still developing their English comprehension.

stories.title: Michigan DNR rescues lake sturgeon from shallow pool near Ontonagon River
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Natural Resources rescued a lake sturgeon from a shallow pool near the Ontonagon River. Recent research suggests these ancient fish can live up to 300 years, challenging previous estimates.

photo.alt: Michigan DNR rescues lake sturgeon from shallow pool near Ontonagon River

stories.title: Michigan Doctors PAC endorses Lisa McIntyre for Michigan's 22nd House District
stories.summary: The Michigan Doctors Political Action Committee endorsed Democratic Michigan 22nd House District nominee Lisa McIntyre.

photo.alt: Michigan Doctors PAC endorses Lisa McIntyre for Michigan's 22nd House District

stories.title: Michigan Enhances Prenatal Care Education and Outreach
stories.summary: The state will expand education and outreach efforts to encourage women of childbearing age to seek early pregnancy confirmation and initiate prenatal care. Programs will focus on reducing barriers to care, promoting best practices, and tracking birth outcomes related to substance exposure and preventable diseases.

stories.title: Michigan environmental news: State announces $89 million for Detroit, Kalamazoo river cleanup
stories.summary: Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer unveiled an $89-million “Reclaiming the Rivers” program to address pollution in the Detroit and Kalamazoo rivers. The funds come from a Monsanto PCB settlement and a 2019 Kalamazoo sediment release settlement. $50 million targets Detroit River sediment, $25 million funds Kalamazoo watershed restoration, and $14 million creates a statewide fund.

photo.alt: Michigan environmental news: State announces $89 million for Detroit, Kalamazoo river cleanup

stories.title: Michigan Expands Fetal Alcohol Syndrome Outreach and Prevention
stories.summary: The state will continue developing outreach programs focused on fetal alcohol syndrome services, including health promotion, prevention, and intervention. The department will also explore federal grants to reduce alcohol and marijuana use among pregnant women.

stories.title: Michigan Forecast: Next weather change just starting to show up. Watch Torregrossa’s live weather update
stories.summary: The weather forecast for Michigan highlights continued fall sunshine and warm afternoons through mid-next week, followed by recurring strong cold fronts every three to four days. Residents are encouraged to watch live updates and forecasts on MLive's weather page.

stories.summary: The weather forecast for Michigan predicts small showers in the southern regions, with otherwise pleasant conditions for September. Viewers are encouraged to watch Mark Torregrossa's live weather update for more details.

stories.title: Michigan foster kids struggle under system that gives ‘nothing’ after aging out
stories.summary: A growing chorus of lawmakers and advocates say Michigan is not doing nearly enough to help the state’s roughly 9,000 foster children after they leave the system. Other states are trying to do it better.

photo.alt: Bridge Listens Issues Watch recap: The challenges rural governments face

stories.title: Michigan Funds $250K Study on Uterine Fibroid Services
stories.summary: The state will allocate $250,000.00 to commission a study evaluating options to expand detection, treatment, and awareness of uterine fibroids, with results to be reported within 30 days of receipt.

stories.title: Michigan Funds National Board Certification Incentives for Teachers
stories.summary: $2.5 million is allocated for National Board Certified teachers through a work project appropriation. Teachers receive $4,000 base awards with an additional $6,000 for those in Title I schools. The project aims to encourage certification and lapses unspent funds by September 30, 2029.

stories.title: Michigan Gas Prices continue climb while diesel sets new all-time record
stories.summary: The average diesel price in Michigan has reached $6.78, with some stations hitting $7, setting a new record. Rising oil prices and a refinery outage in Illinois are contributing to the increase, which also affects airfare and business operations.

photo.alt: Michigan Gas Prices continue climb while diesel sets new all-time record

stories.title: Michigan gas prices soar to $4.89, some Metro Detroit stations top $5
stories.summary: Gas prices in Michigan have risen to an average of $4.89 per gallon, with some Metro Detroit stations exceeding $5. Diesel fuel averages $6.67 per gallon, driven by global demand and a refinery outage in Illinois. The war in Iran has significantly contributed to the increase, nearly doubling the national average since February 28, 2026.
