stories.title: Michigan got $173M to transform rural health. Where is it going?
stories.summary: Michigan is distributing $173 million in federal grants through the Rural Health Transformation Program to improve rural healthcare. Stakeholders argue the funds are insufficient to address Medicaid cuts and facility stability, with concerns that money is flowing to peripheral programs rather than hospitals. The state plans to allocate funds across four initiatives, but reporting transparency issues have emerged as budget deadlines approach.

photo.alt: State health officials discuss Rural Health Transformation Program progress with a Michigan House Appropriations Subcommittee on Sept. 22, 2026. (Eli Newman/Bridge Michigan)

stories.title: Michigan got $173M to transform rural health. Where is it going?
stories.summary: Michigan is distributing $173 million in federal grants through the Rural Health Transformation Program to improve rural healthcare. The funds will support initiatives like chronic condition collaboration, workforce training, home-based services, and technology upgrades. However, rural healthcare leaders and lawmakers express concerns about insufficient funding for critical areas and demand greater transparency in allocation.

photo.alt: a shot of the back of a seated woman testifying before a legislative committee.

stories.title: Michigan got $173m to transform rural health: Where is it going?
stories.summary: Michigan faces a reporting lag in tracking $173 million in Rural Health Transformation funding, with only $1.9 million encumbered so far. State officials highlight transparency issues and a need for clear performance metrics to ensure continued funding, as the state must obligate funds by October 30 and spend them by September 2027.

photo.alt: Michigan got $173m to transform rural health: Where is it going?

stories.title: Michigan governor race: Where candidates stand on school policy
stories.summary: Chris Swanson outlines a seven-point education plan prioritizing free school meals for all students, expanded preschool access, and directing state School Aid Fund to K-12 schools. He opposes replicating Mississippi's education model, arguing Michigan students are performing better than national test data suggests and advocating for an assessment of the state's education system if elected.

photo.alt: Michigan governor race: Where candidates stand on school policy

stories.title: Michigan gubernatorial candidates debate trade wars, data centers, health care, and more
stories.summary: Michigan’s major party gubernatorial candidates, Democrat Jocelyn Benson and Republican John James, debated issues including trade wars, education, and energy during a WOOD-TV-hosted event in Grand Rapids. Benson criticized James for aligning with President Trump’s policies, while James emphasized breaking from the administration on trade and Iran. The debate also covered education reforms and gas tax suspensions amid rising fuel prices.

photo.alt: Republican John James and Democrat Jocelyn Benson stand at their lecterns during a gubernatorial debate on Oct. 6, 2026.

stories.title: Michigan gubernatorial candidates debate key issues
stories.summary: Democratic candidate Jocelyn Benson and Republican candidate John James debated topics including data center moratoriums, gas taxes, and Medicaid access. The next debate is scheduled for Oct. 15.

photo.alt: Outlier Media newsletter image

stories.title: Michigan high school teacher receives surprise $75K excellence award
stories.summary: Clio High School teacher Matthew McMullen was awarded $75,000 as a winner of the 2026 Harbor Freight Tools for Schools Prize for Teaching Excellence. The award recognizes skilled trades educators and includes classroom upgrades. McMullen plans to use the funds to replace welders and improve his wood shop.

photo.alt: Teacher receiving award with students and staff present

stories.title: Michigan House bill would give school credit for job experience
stories.summary: The bill would require school districts to grant credit to seniors who work at least 30 hours a week in manufacturing, construction, or other fields that provide verifiable job training.

photo.alt: Podcast title 'That's What They Say' with hosts Anne Curzan & Rebecca Hector

stories.title: Michigan House committee probes canvassing process amid dispute over citizen-only voting signatures
stories.summary: The Michigan House Select Committee on the Rules and Procedures of the State Board of Canvassers and the Bureau of Elections is investigating the canvassing process following the failure of a citizen-only voting initiative. The effort, which aimed to require citizenship verification for voting, was rejected on August 24 after a partisan deadlock on the Board of State Canvassers. Proponents plan to reattempt the initiative in 2028 and criticized the Bureau of Elections' signature validation process as unfair.

photo.alt: Image related to Michigan voting initiative

stories.title: Michigan Increases Insurance Provider Assessment Revenue by $7.414M
stories.summary: State restricted insurance provider assessment revenue, as appropriated in 2025 PA 22, is increased by $7,414,400. This adjustment boosts funding for insurance provider assessments in healthcare programs.

stories.title: Michigan is burning. Here’s what the next governor can do to extinguish the blaze.
stories.summary: The Detroit Regional Chamber has not endorsed either gubernatorial candidate, Jocelyn Benson or John James, due to their failure to secure a two-thirds majority vote from its PAC. The article argues that Michigan's next governor must prioritize education and economic development strategies to address the state's economic challenges, including boosting post-secondary credentials and transforming the state's economic development approach. The current gubernatorial race has been overshadowed by the U.S. Senate contest, with neither candidate adequately addressing long-term economic issues like workforce aging and talent retention.

photo.alt: U.S. Rep. John James, R-Shelby Twp., speaks at the Mackinac Policy Conference on Mackinac Island, Mich., on May 27, 2026. (Photo by Andrew Roth/Michigan Advance)

stories.title: Michigan Journalists of the Year
stories.summary: Jonathan Oosting and Mike Wilkinson were named Michigan Journalists of the Year for the fourth consecutive year. Their work exposed issues in Michigan's grant-making process, including a controversial $25 million health campus linked to a former House Speaker, and highlighted safety lapses at Michigan State University following a campus mass shooting.

stories.title: Michigan Launches Digital Credentialing Initiative for CTE Programs
stories.summary: $3 million is allocated for a statewide digital credentialing initiative supporting CTE programs. The program creates verifiable digital records of skills for students and educators to enhance workforce competitiveness through improved skills transparency and portability.

stories.title: Michigan launches project with crop insurance companies to reward regenerative farming
stories.summary: About 80 farmers in Michigan's thumb region will participate in a pilot project recognizing lower crop loss risks from regenerative farming techniques.

photo.alt: A grayscale image of a hand placing a ballot into a ballot box in front of the U.S. Supreme Court building, with trees in the background. The It’s Just Politics logo appears in the upper right corner.

stories.title: Michigan lawmakers, state leaders announce $89M for Detroit and Kalamazoo River cleanup
stories.summary: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer and state officials announced an $89 million investment to clean up and restore the Detroit and Kalamazoo rivers, part of the Reclaim the Rivers initiative. The funding will address PCB contamination, support river restoration projects, and build on existing cleanup efforts involving federal agencies, tribal governments, and private partners.

photo.alt: Michigan lawmakers, state leaders announce $89M for Detroit and Kalamazoo River cleanup

stories.title: Michigan League of Handweavers’ 23rd Biennial Fiber Show showcases diverse craftsmanship
stories.summary: From weaving to doll-making, a broad range of craftsmanship will be featured in both exhibitions and public demonstrations at the Michigan League of Handweavers’ 23rd Biennial Fiber Show.

stories.title: Michigan Legislature Allocates $300 Million for Postsecondary Scholarship Fund in 2026 Budget
stories.summary: The Michigan Legislature has allocated $300 million for the postsecondary scholarship fund for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026, with $200 million from the state school aid fund and $100 million from the general fund. The legislature intends for this fund to be the primary source for the Michigan achievement scholarship, aiming to increase annual deposits until fully implementing the scholarship's costs. If funding shortfalls occur, additional appropriations from the scholarship fund will be used, requiring notification to higher education committees.

stories.title: Michigan Legislature to Submit Joint List of Legislatively Directed Spending Items
stories.summary: The Michigan Senate and House must jointly submit a list of legislatively directed spending items within 30 days of the budget act's enactment. The list must include all publicly disclosed information about funded items, as required by the Management and Budget Act.

stories.title: Michigan Libertarian Party disavows its own gubernatorial nominee
stories.summary: The Michigan Libertarian Party released a statement disavowing Anthony Hudson, its gubernatorial candidate, claiming his ideology contradicts the party's core values. Hudson responded by disavowing party insiders, stating his campaign was about serving the people, not the party. Despite the disavowal, Hudson's name remains on the Libertarian Party line for the November election.

photo.alt: Anthony Hudson speaking to the Mason City Council on February 2, 2026

stories.title: Michigan Libertarian Party disavows its own gubernatorial nominee
stories.summary: The Michigan Libertarian Party released a statement disavowing Anthony Hudson, its gubernatorial nominee, claiming his ideology contradicts the party's core values. Hudson, a Genesee County truck driver, responded by disavowing the party's priorities and stating he would rather stand alone than surrender his principles. Despite the disavowal, Hudson's name remains on the Libertarian Party line for the November election.

photo.alt: Michigan Libertarian Party disavows its own gubernatorial nominee

stories.title: Michigan Libertarian party washes its hands of its gubernatorial nominee
stories.summary: The Libertarian Party of Michigan has disavowed its gubernatorial nominee Anthony Hudson after leadership censured him for using a homophobic slur, anti-Muslim language, and supporting Trump's military actions. Hudson responded with profanity and criticized the party's positions on LGBTQ rights and drug legalization. The party will no longer support his campaign but acknowledges he remains the official candidate.

photo.alt: Anthony Hudson. (Steve Carmody / Michigan Public )

stories.title: Michigan Libertarian party washes its hands of its gubernatorial nominee
stories.summary: The Michigan Libertarian Party has disavowed its gubernatorial nominee Anthony Hudson after censuring him earlier this month, disassociating from his campaign entirely.

stories.title: Michigan Libraries Receive $750,000 for State Aid and eLibrary Expansion
stories.summary: $375,000 will be added to state aid for public libraries, with another $375,000 allocated for expanding the Michigan eLibrary's free online access to research materials. Funds will be distributed under the State Aid to Public Libraries Act.

stories.title: Michigan man among 7 named in Cornell fraternity sexual assault lawsuit
stories.summary: A St. Clair County, Michigan man and former Cornell University student is accused in a lawsuit of participating in the 2024 drugging and sexual assault of a female student at the Chi Phi fraternity house. The lawsuit, filed in September 2026, names seven individuals, Cornell University, and Greek organizations, alleging the victim was incapable of consent. The case has prompted a reopened criminal investigation by New York’s Tompkins County DA.

photo.alt: Gavel MLive

stories.title: Michigan man among fraternity members sued in Cornell assault case
stories.summary: A woman who formerly attended Cornell University has sued the school, a bar, several Greek organizations, and seven fraternity members, including a Michigan man, in connection with a 2024 sexual assault. The lawsuit, filed on Sept. 16, 2026, accuses the men of assaulting the woman while she was intoxicated at a fraternity house. Attorney Jeremy Saland, representing one of the accused, Scott Kretzschmar, denied the allegations, stating documents corroborate his client's position and disprove the claims.

photo.alt: Portrait of Jalen Williams

stories.title: Michigan Mandates Literacy Coaching and Intervention by 2027-2028
stories.summary: The state requires school districts to provide technical assistance for reporting pupil reading improvement plans by the 2027-2028 school year. District-identified literacy coaches must focus on intervention instruction rather than classroom teaching.

stories.title: Michigan Mandates Literacy-Focused Teacher Certification Test
stories.summary: The state requires the adoption of a teacher certification test ensuring elementary teachers can deliver evidence-based literacy instruction grounded in the science of reading.

stories.title: Michigan Mandates Precontract Risk Assessments for State Department Contractors
stories.summary: A new policy requires the department to conduct precontract risk assessments for financial, security, and insurance risks before executing contracts. A report on these assessments and executed contracts must be submitted by March 31, 2027.

stories.title: Michigan manufacturing
stories.summary: Trump's 'Build America Plan' focused on manufacturing growth through tariffs. Michigan gained 5,000 manufacturing jobs since Trump's second term began, with General Motors and other automakers shifting production to the US. The administration is also steering defense contracts to autoworkers and lowering fuel economy standards to boost profits.

stories.title: Michigan manufacturing revival
stories.summary: Trump's 'Build America Plan' aimed to boost manufacturing through tariffs. Michigan gained 5,000 manufacturing jobs since January 2025, with GM and Toyota expanding production. The Trump administration lowered fuel economy standards and used the Defense Production Act to direct contracts to automakers.

photo.alt: Donald Trump smiling on a stage. Supporters are cheering him on.

stories.title: Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund Appropriation
stories.summary: For the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026, $45,000,000 is appropriated for certain capital outlay projects from the Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund. The adjusted gross appropriation remains at $45,000,000 with no interdepartmental grants, federal revenues, or local revenues specified.

stories.title: Michigan orchards are open. Where to find cider and donuts this fall
stories.summary: Michigan's apple orchards are in full swing, offering fresh cider, donuts, and fall activities. Visitors can enjoy picking apples and seasonal treats at various orchards across the state.

stories.title: Michigan parents charged after son displayed loaded gun at daycare
stories.summary: Two parents have been charged with misdemeanor crimes after their 3-year-old son displayed a loaded gun at a suburban Detroit daycare.

stories.title: Michigan parents got Facebook message saying son was lost. What video shows about his bus dropoff
stories.summary: Airport Community Schools Superintendent Ryan Duvall addressed an incident where parents received a Facebook message claiming their son was lost during a bus dropoff. The district filed a report with local law enforcement and emphasized that student transportation is managed by third-party vendor First Student, which retains responsibility for its employees. Administration is collaborating with First Student to review procedures and ensure driver protocols are followed, though the vendor has not yet responded to inquiries about preventive measures.

stories.title: Michigan Passes FY27 General Omnibus Appropriations Bill SB 878 PA 21 of 2026
stories.summary: Michigan's 103rd Legislature approved Senate Bill 878 on July 21, 2026, to make, supplement, adjust, and consolidate appropriations for state departments, agencies, and capital outlay purposes for fiscal years ending September 30, 2026, and 2027. The bill includes $135.6 million in adjusted gross appropriations for the Department of Agriculture and Rural Development for FY2027. Introduced by Senator Anthony, the act provides funding conditions and expenditure guidelines while repealing previous acts.

stories.title: Michigan PFAS Awareness Week is a call to action
stories.summary: Michigan's PFAS Awareness Week highlights the dangers of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in the state's environment and water supply. The week-long event, declared by Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, encourages residents to reduce PFAS exposure while addressing new threats from data centers that use these chemicals. Advocates call for stricter regulations and corporate accountability to prevent further contamination.

photo.alt: Image related to PFAS awareness and water contamination

stories.title: Michigan private schools could lose tax exemption over race-based policies
stories.summary: Michigan private schools may face losing their tax-exempt status if they maintain race-based policies, as the state considers new legislation targeting such practices. The proposed changes aim to address disparities in tax benefits for educational institutions.

photo.alt: Michigan private schools could lose tax exemption over race-based policies

stories.title: Michigan Professional Firefighters Union and National Security Leaders for America endorse Jocelyn Benson
stories.summary: The Michigan Professional Firefighters Union and National Security Leaders for America endorsed Democratic Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson's gubernatorial campaign.

stories.title: Michigan progressive rabbis use Harris visit to press El-Sayed on 'nonnegotiable' Jewish concerns
stories.summary: A group of Michigan rabbis, part of Nonnegotiable Michigan, issued an open letter to Kamala Harris urging her to push Abdul El-Sayed to address Jewish safety and identity concerns. The rabbis criticized El-Sayed's stance on Israel and his campaign's association with Hasan Piker, requesting a meeting that he has yet to accept.

photo.alt: Kamala Harris and Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan

stories.title: Michigan Provides Technical Assistance for Medicaid Mental Health Funding
stories.summary: At least $159,500 and 1.0 FTE position will support technical assistance for eligible districts to effectively use Medicaid funds for mental health services.

stories.title: Michigan Public names Brian Manzullo as managing editor of multiplatform news strategy
stories.summary: Michigan Public has appointed Brian Manzullo as its inaugural managing editor of multiplatform news strategy. Manzullo brings over 14 years of experience from the Detroit Free Press and The Arizona Republic to his new role, where he will strengthen the station's digital journalism and expand its reach across platforms. He will start on September 21, 2026, based in Ann Arbor.

photo.alt: Brian Manzullo headshot

stories.title: Michigan Public Service Commission Mandated to Provide Monthly Utility Rate Data
stories.summary: The Michigan Public Service Commission must submit a report by September 30 summarizing public hearings on utility issues and outages. It will also provide monthly utility rate data, reliability metrics, and complaint statistics online, including a dedicated webpage for pending rate cases with projected impacts for residential customers.

stories.title: Michigan rabbis push El-Sayed to change rhetoric on Israel, ensure safety of Jewish community
stories.summary: Michigan Jewish rabbis and leaders have launched Nonnegotiable Michigan, a coalition representing 40,000 Jewish voters, demanding Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed affirm commitments to Jewish safety, identity, and political participation. The group calls its demands an 'invitation' for El-Sayed to address concerns ahead of the Nov. 3 general election, as tensions rise over his rhetoric on Israel and Gaza. El-Sayed's campaign claims he is working to mend ties with the Jewish community through meetings and public commitments to safety.

photo.alt: Michigan rabbis push El-Sayed to change rhetoric on Israel, ensure safety of Jewish community

stories.title: Michigan-raised Nashville bluegrass artist sharing new album at The Ark show
stories.summary: Bluegrass artist Lindsay Lou will perform at an upcoming show in Ann Arbor on Oct. 4 at The Ark to share the release of her new album, Bluegrass Women. The album, released on Aug. 14, celebrates women's contributions to bluegrass and features collaborations with artists like Molly Tuttle and Sierra Hull. The show starts at 7:30 p.m. with tickets starting at $29.

photo.alt: Bluegrass artist Lindsay Lou will perform at an upcoming show in Ann Arbor on Oct. 4 at The Ark to share the release of her new album, Bluegrass Women. Photo provided by Sydney Griffin with permission to use.

stories.title: Michigan Reduces Quality Assurance Assessment Program Revenue by $1.978M
stories.summary: State restricted quality assurance assessment program revenue, as appropriated in 2025 PA 22, is reduced by $1,978,400. This adjustment affects funding for quality assurance programs in healthcare.

stories.title: Michigan regulators approve $74.5 million DTE Gas hike, less than half utility’s request
stories.summary: Michigan regulators approved a $74.52 million DTE gas rate hike Thursday — less than half of what the utility requested — raising typical residential bills by 3.34%, or $2.87 monthly, starting Oct. 1. Regulators blocked $284.1 million in costs tied to a compressor station project and require DTE to analyze racial disparities in service shutoffs.

photo.alt: Michigan regulators approve $74.5 million DTE Gas hike, less than half utility’s request

stories.title: Michigan regulators OK DTE contracts for Google data center
stories.summary: Michigan's utility regulator approved DTE Energy contracts to power Google's 1-gigawatt data center in Van Buren Township. The Wayne County Commission overrode a veto for a tax exemption saving Google over $125 million. The contracts require Google to fund renewable energy and storage, with the facility expected to begin service in December 2027.

photo.alt: Michigan regulators OK DTE contracts for Google data center

stories.title: Michigan regulators OK DTE contracts for Google data center
stories.summary: Michigan’s utility regulator voted unanimously to grant conditional approval for DTE Energy contracts to power Google’s 1-gigawatt data center in Van Buren Township. The Wayne County Commission also overrode a veto to grant a tax exemption for the project. The contracts require Google to cover generation, transmission, and distribution costs, with the data center expected to begin service in December 2027.

photo.alt: Data center project image

stories.title: Michigan regulators want to restrain utilities' bias toward building costly power plants
stories.summary: Governor Gretchen Whitmer asked the Michigan Public Service Commission for ideas on lowering utility bills. The commission says the most important way to do that is address 'capital bias.'

stories.title: Michigan Releases 2026 Supplemental Funding Budget Provisions
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Technology, Management, and Budget has outlined new requirements in the 2026 supplemental funding budget, including annual work project account reporting, preferences for Michigan-made goods and veteran-owned businesses, in-person work policies, and space utilization assessments for state agencies. The provisions emphasize accountability, local economic support, and compliance with federal guidelines.

stories.title: Michigan Releases FY2027 State Budget Details with Supplemental Funding Provisions
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget for fiscal year 2027 includes provisions for policy change reporting, federal contingency funds, legacy cost allocations, and work project fund management. Key sections outline requirements for April 1 policy reports, $2.5 million in federal contingency authorization, and $133 million in pension-related legacy costs. The document also mandates preferences for Michigan-made goods and services in state expenditures.

stories.title: Michigan Releases FY27 General Omnibus Budget Bill with Supplemental Funding for 2026
stories.summary: Michigan's FY27 General Omnibus Budget Bill allocates $34.7 million for pension-related legacy costs through 2027. The bill mandates exhausting existing work project funds before new appropriations, requires biannual work project account reports, prioritizes Michigan-made goods/services including veteran-owned businesses, enforces in-person work policies with 80% occupancy targets, and establishes space utilization assessments by July 1, 2027. It also promotes contracting with geographically disadvantaged businesses.

stories.title: Michigan Releases FY27 Supplemental Budget with $109.6 Million in Appropriations
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget for Fiscal Year 2027 includes $109.6 million in supplemental funding across departments, including child care, Medicaid mental health services, and state police programs. The budget emphasizes compliance with federal regulations and reallocation of American Rescue Plan Act funds to ensure full expenditure by December 31, 2026. Provisions also address fiscal recovery fund management and audit requirements.

stories.title: Michigan reopens review of Line 5 tunnel permits following Supreme Court decision
stories.summary: Michigan regulators will reconsider permits for Enbridge’s Line 5 oil tunnel after the state Supreme Court ruled environmental impacts must be weighed before approval. Gov. Whitmer urged Enbridge to abandon the project, while tribes and environmental groups praised the decision.

photo.alt: Michigan reopens review of Line 5 tunnel permits following Supreme Court decision

stories.title: Michigan Repeals and Amends Sections of State School Aid Act of 1979
stories.summary: The text outlines the repeal of multiple sections from the 1979 State School Aid Act and the enactment of amendments. Some provisions take immediate effect, while others are scheduled for October 1, 2026. The act is ordered to take immediate effect under Article IV of the Michigan Constitution.

stories.title: Michigan Replaces Federal Funding Cuts for School Health Programs
stories.summary: Funds appropriated for adolescent and school health will replace federal funding reductions from the HHS-CDC and the state school aid act.

stories.title: Michigan Requires Grant Recipients to Submit Detailed Reports by September 1
stories.summary: The state mandates that grantees submit a report by September 1 of the current fiscal year, including audited financial statements, education and clinical quality data, trainee rosters, and Medicaid revenue by training site.

stories.title: Michigan Requires Medicaid Pharmaceutical Cost and Rebate Report by May 15
stories.summary: The department must submit a report by May 15 detailing Medicaid pharmaceutical costs, rebates, and related expenses for the previous fiscal year and first two quarters of the current year.

stories.title: Michigan Requires Updated Reading Assessments by August 2027
stories.summary: By August 1, 2027, school districts must update their reading assessments to include universal screening tools for dyslexia, minimizing instructional time impact through approved assessments.

stories.title: Michigan research council predicts legal challenges if money-out-of-politics campaign succeeds
stories.summary: A campaign to restrict political contributions by big utilities and state contractors faces potential legal challenges due to U.S. Supreme Court rulings protecting corporate campaign speech.

stories.title: Michigan's 10th Congressional District Race
stories.summary: Coverage of Michigan's 10th Congressional District race, where voters in Macomb County will select a successor to Republican John James, includes an extended conversation with an Oakland University professor on civic dialogue.

photo.alt: Michigan's 10th Congressional District Race

stories.title: Michigan’s 96th House District race: Bridge issues dominate debate
stories.summary: Incumbent Republican Timmy Beson and Democratic challenger Chris Girard clashed over bridge access, tolls, and infrastructure during their debate for Michigan’s 96th House District. Beson emphasized local bridge funding and small business concerns, while Girard focused on affordability, cost-of-living challenges, and seeking state-level solutions for bridge control and oversight.

photo.alt: Timmy Beson, left, and Chris Girard, right.MLive graphic

stories.title: Michigan’s chronic absenteeism rate, once among the highest in the nation, falls for fourth year
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District continued to see improvements in its chronic absenteeism rate, which was at 60% at the end of the 2025-26 school year.

photo.alt: Michigan’s chronic absenteeism rate, once among the highest in the nation, falls for fourth year

stories.title: Michigan's felony murder law disproportionately impacts Black residents
stories.summary: A new analysis reveals Black Michiganders are convicted of felony murder at three times the rate of white residents. The charge can apply when someone is involved in a crime where a death occurs, even if they weren't present. Advocates hope Michigan will follow Pennsylvania's lead in banning mandatory life sentences for felony murder.

photo.alt: Michigan's felony murder law disproportionately impacts Black residents

stories.title: Michigan's FY27 Budget Bill Includes New Reporting, Procurement, and Workforce Policies
stories.summary: The FY27 General Omnibus Bill (SB 878/PA 21 of 2026) establishes requirements for work project account reporting, prioritizes Michigan-made goods in state contracts, mandates in-person workforce policies, and requires space utilization assessments for state agencies. The bill also includes provisions for geographically disadvantaged business enterprises and federal policy impact reporting.

stories.title: Michigan's PFAS Awareness Week Highlights Data Center Threats to Water Safety
stories.summary: Michigan's PFAS Awareness Week (Sept. 21-25) highlights the state's over 300 PFAS-contaminated sites and emerging threats from proposed data centers that could introduce new PFAS pollution through refrigerants and cable coatings. Clean water advocates are urging stronger regulations to address all PFAS chemicals and hold polluters accountable for cleanup costs, as low-income communities already burdened by legacy contamination face new risks.

photo.alt: A person holding a water sample with a droplet highlighting contamination concerns.

stories.title: Michigan’s sex offender registry shrank by nearly half. Here’s why.
stories.summary: A state supreme court ruling is sparking a major debate over constitutional rights and public safety as more than 20,000 sex offenders are being removed from Michigan’s registry. Michigan State Police have removed over 20,000 people from the registry following a landmark court decision that invalidated retroactive registration requirements for offenses before July 1, 2011.

photo.alt: Michigan’s sex offender registry shrank by nearly half. Here’s why.

stories.title: Michigan’s suicide death rates are declining, council recommends more prevention efforts
stories.summary: Michigan's suicide rate has decreased since 2017, according to a 2024 report by the Michigan Suicide Prevention Council. The council recommends sustaining state funding for prevention infrastructure and educating professionals on risk assessment. Factors like firearm access, unemployment, and social isolation contribute to suicide risk.

photo.alt: Michigan’s suicide death rates are declining, council recommends more prevention efforts

stories.title: Michigan's Tenth Congressional race could determine which party controls Congress
stories.summary: The district, which represents parts of Macomb and Oakland Counties, has leaned Republican in the past, but the race between Michael Bouchard and Christina Hines is considered a toss-up.

photo.alt: democrat and republican

stories.title: Michigan's Tunnel of Trees is a fall favorite. Is it still detoured?
stories.summary: Michigan's Tunnel of Trees, M-119 between Harbor Springs and Cross Village, remains partially closed for repairs due to spring and summer runoff. Sections near Division Road and Devil's Elbow are detoured until 2027 and indefinitely, respectively, while one segment reopened recently. The scenic drive is a popular fall attraction despite current closures.

stories.title: Michigan’s two major party candidates for U.S. Senate offer differing ideas for health care
stories.summary: Republican Mike Rogers rolls out plan heavy on transparency; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed advocates for Medicare for All

stories.title: Michigan’s Two Major Party Candidates for U.S. Senate Offer Differing Ideas for Health Care
stories.summary: The two U.S. senate candidates from Michigan offer vastly different ideas for health care. Lowering costs for consumers is the goal for both.

photo.alt: Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers speaks to reporters at a campaign office in Taylor, Michigan on Saturday, September 19.

stories.title: Michigan says plastic surgeon poses an ‘immediate threat’: Here’s what we know
stories.summary: A Metro Detroit plastic surgeon’s medical license has been suspended in three states, including Michigan, after allegations of misconduct. Dr. Ayoub Sayeg, whose license was suspended in late September, is accused of posing an 'immediate threat to public health, safety, or welfare.' A patient claims he left her permanently disfigured, and his now-deleted Instagram page showcased his work with over 50,000 procedures claimed.

stories.title: Michigan school districts, food pantries feel SNAP cut ripple effect ahead of cost shift to states
stories.summary: Michigan school districts and food pantries are experiencing the ripple effects of federal SNAP benefit cuts as states prepare to assume higher administrative costs starting October 1. Analysts estimate the state will face a $95 million cost increase in the first year, with over 167,000 residents including 53,000 children losing benefits. Food pantry leaders report rising demand, while school officials warn that reduced SNAP eligibility could jeopardize free meal programs as state funding burdens grow.

stories.title: Michigan secretary of state candidates weigh in on election transparency, Trump administration

Forlini prioritizes clean voter rolls, while Gilchrist focuses on protecting elections from federal interference. Both will debate on October 8 in Ann Arbor.

stories.title: Michigan secretary of state hopefuls discuss election security, office priorities
stories.summary: Candidates for Michigan Secretary of State participated in an online forum hosted by the League of Women Voters of Michigan on Sept. 29, 2026, discussing election security, misinformation, and office priorities. The five nominees from major and minor parties addressed topics including voter data protection, election integrity, rural access to services, and data privacy. Responses highlighted ideological differences on issues like federal data sharing, electronic voting systems, and voter registration processes.

stories.title: Michigan secretary of state hopefuls discuss election security, office priorities

The candidates included Lt. Gov. Garlin Gilchrist (D), Macomb County Clerk Anthony Forlini (R), and minor-party nominees Eric Borregard (Green), Christine Sloan (Libertarian), and Scott Aughney (Taxpayers Party). stories.title: Michigan selects official Christmas tree for holiday season
stories.summary: Michigan has selected a 60-foot spruce donated by the Larry Riccio family from Iron Mountain as the state's official Christmas tree. The tree will be cut down on Nov. 5 and transported to the state Capitol in Lansing, where it will be prepared for a tree-lighting ceremony during the 42nd annual Silver Bells in the City celebration on Nov. 20.

stories.title: Michigan Sen. Gary Peters' election history
stories.summary: Peters was first elected to the U.S. Senate in 2014, defeating Terri Lynn Land 55%-41%, and re-elected in 2020, defeating John James 49.9%-48.2%.

stories.title: Michigan Sen. Gary Peters to join USC political center. When he starts
stories.summary: Michigan Senator Gary Peters, known for his political career spanning local and state offices, is set to join the USC political center. stories.title: Michigan Sen. Gary Peters to lead USC political center. What he'll do
stories.summary: After completing his Senate term in January 2027, U.S. Sen. Gary Peters will co-lead one of the only political centers in the country jointly led by a Democrat and a Republican. Peters will become the Carmen H. and Louis Warschaw Endowed Chair in Practical Politics at the University of Southern California and serve as director of the Center for the Political Future at the USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences alongside Republican strategist Mike Murphy.

stories.summary: Michigan Sen. Chedrick Greene (D-Saginaw) introduced Senate Bill 1186, which would require the state to reimburse local governments for costs incurred during special legislative elections. The bill faces bipartisan support and criticism, with concerns about potential incentives for delayed elections and the financial burden on local clerks. The committee heard testimony but did not vote on the legislation.

stories.title: Michigan Senate seat up for grabs between former state rep, local party chair
stories.summary: Voters in Michigan Senate District 15 will elect a new state senator in the Nov. 3 general election. The race pits former state representative Felicia Brabec (D-Pittsfield Township) against Republican Jason Rogers, chair of the Washtenaw GOP. Both candidates qualified after primary elections in August, with Brabec defeating fellow Democrat Michael White and Rogers running uncontested. Current term-limited Sen. Jeff Irwin (D-Ann Arbor) is not seeking re-election.

stories.title: Michigan seniors share secrets to living to 100
stories.summary: Michigan centenarians shared their secrets to living to 100 during a ceremony at a luncheon. They emphasized enjoying life and having fun, while Canton Township Supervisor Anne Marie Graham-Hudak presented proclamations to the honorees. The event highlighted their roles as family members, caregivers, and community contributors beyond being historical witnesses.

stories.title: Michigan set to open new $383 million psychiatric hospital in Northville
stories.summary: Michigan is opening a new $383 million psychiatric hospital in Northville, which will transfer patients from the Walter P. Reuther Hospital in Westland. The 264-bed facility, built on the former Hawthorn Center site, increases the state's capacity by 54 beds, totaling 730 beds statewide. The hospital features geothermal heating/cooling, outdoor courtyards, and specialized spaces for patient care.

stories.title: Michigan sheriff’s office took man’s lawful pistol, kept it indefinitely, lawsuit says
stories.summary: A Taylor man filed a federal lawsuit against the Livingston County Sheriff’s Office after deputies seized his lawful Heckler & Koch VP9 pistol and 18 rounds of ammunition during an August 25 traffic stop in Brighton Township. The lawsuit claims the deputies took the weapon without evidence it was illegal, stolen, or that the owner posed a danger, solely because its serial number wasn't in a law enforcement database.

stories.title: Michigan Smart Trade Alliance tracker shows over $26 billion in tariff-driven costs paid statewide
stories.summary: The Michigan Smart Trade Alliance has launched a tracker estimating Michigan households have incurred over $26 billion in tariff-related costs since January 2025, or about $6,419 per household. The estimate uses data from the National Taxpayers Union Foundation, though other analysts and the White House provide lower figures. The alliance advocates for ending trade policies they claim raise costs and hinder economic planning.

stories.title: Michigan State Budget Director to Ensure Expenditure of Fiscal Recovery Funds by December 31, 2026
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget director must ensure all state fiscal recovery funds from the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 are expended by December 31, 2026. Funds at risk of lapsing after September 30, 2026, will be automatically reappropriated for the same purpose through December 31, 2026.

stories.title: Michigan State Budget Includes New Work Project Reporting and Procurement Requirements
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget for FY27 includes provisions requiring annual reports on work project accounts, prioritizing Michigan-made goods and services, enforcing in-person work policies, and assessing federal policy impacts. Agencies must submit space utilization assessments by July 2027 and optimize office space usage. The budget also mandates reporting on federal guidelines affecting department operations by December 2026 and June 2027.

stories.title: Michigan State Budget Requires Expenditure of ARPA Funds by December 2026
stories.summary: The state budget director must ensure all American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds allocated to Michigan under Public Law 117-2 are fully expended by December 31, 2026. Funds that would otherwise lapse after September 30, 2026, are automatically reappropriated for the same purpose until the deadline.

stories.title: Michigan State Department to Complete Space Utilization Assessment by July 1
stories.summary: The Michigan state department is required to complete a space utilization assessment by July 1 using a form developed by the Department of Technology, Management, and Budget. The assessment will cover all space assigned under building occupancy agreements and leased office locations, with plans to optimize space usage.

stories.title: Michigan State Department to Prioritize State-Owned Facilities in Space Optimization
stories.summary: The Michigan state department must develop a plan to reduce, consolidate, or optimize assigned space, prioritizing state-owned facilities. The plan must comply with space standards established by the Department of Technology, Management, and Budget unless exceptions are approved.

stories.title: Michigan State Department to Report on Federal Policy Impacts by December 31, 2026
stories.summary: The Michigan state department must submit a report by December 31, 2026, detailing federal guidelines, rules, or policy changes (including H.R. 1 and the Rural Health Transformation Program) that significantly impact its operations. The report will address changes in federal revenue and their effects on public health and welfare.

stories.title: Michigan State Fiscal Recovery Funds Expenditure Plan
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget director is required to ensure all state fiscal recovery funds from the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 are spent by December 31, 2026. Unexpended funds after September 30, 2026 will be automatically reappropriated until that deadline. The act also outlines reallocation procedures for funds at risk of missing deadlines, including redirecting them to public health and safety employee payroll and benefits.

stories.title: Michigan state House committee hears testimony over concerns about ballot initiative process
stories.summary: A state House committee in Michigan is examining ways to improve the ballot initiative process after a conservative-backed measure failed to qualify for the ballot. Americans for Citizen Voting (ACV) submitted over 700,000 signatures but was disqualified due to insufficient valid signatures, with the group criticizing delays and lack of transparency in the review process. The committee emphasized it is focused on procedural improvements rather than political outcomes.

stories.summary: Michigan State University moved most classes to remote instruction following a widespread power outage on Sept. 19 that left buildings without hot water. President Kevin M. Guskiewicz called the situation 'unprecedented' and said restoration could take up to a week, with 24 buildings requiring additional cleanup.

stories.title: Michigan State University shifts to online classes after power outage
stories.summary: Michigan State University has transitioned to online instruction and remote work through Sept. 21, 2026, following a power outage that disrupted hot water and other services on the East Lansing campus. The outage began when a central connection point at the T.B. Simon Power Plant failed, prompting university leaders to reduce strain on systems while crews work to restore services. President Kevin M. Guskiewicz emphasized the university's priority of community safety and wellbeing during the ongoing response.

stories.summary: An audit found that Michigan's child welfare system still has serious caseload issues, with one case going more than three years without a primary worker listed in the state’s tracking system.

stories.title: Michigan Strategic Fund looks to future of battery, auto parts supply industry
stories.summary: The Michigan Strategic Fund revised incentives for battery maker Our Next Energy, reducing state funding from $200 million to $150 million and adjusting job commitments and timelines. The company has shifted focus to grid storage and defense contracts amid EV market challenges. The fund also expanded a program to support auto parts suppliers in transitioning to EV and diversified supply chains.

stories.title: Michigan student literacy bills cleared a House committee Wednesday
stories.summary: A Michigan House committee approved several bills aimed at improving literacy in schools, including requirements for teacher training in the science of reading and support for students with dyslexia. The legislation now moves to the full House for consideration. State and national exams show significant challenges for Michigan students in reading proficiency.

stories.title: Michigan student literacy bills cleared a House committee Wednesday
stories.summary: The Michigan House committee passed three literacy bills aimed at improving reading instruction and dyslexia support. The legislation requires teacher training in the science of reading, mandates literacy methods for K-5 teachers, and ensures dyslexia support through Orton-Gillingham training. Testimonies highlighted the need for these measures to address gaps in literacy education.

stories.title: Michigan sues Blue Cross Blue Shield over alleged insurance monopoly
stories.summary: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel announced a federal lawsuit against Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan, alleging the insurer operates an illegal health insurance monopoly. Nessel claims the company has driven up costs while degrading healthcare quality across the state.

stories.title: Michigan Supreme Court blocks proof-of-citizenship voting measure
stories.summary: The Michigan Supreme Court blocked a November ballot measure requiring proof of citizenship to vote, but voters will decide on a proposal to restrict utility spending on political campaigns. Fact-checks are available to help voters understand the issues.

stories.title: Michigan Supreme Court orders review of Oxford school shooter's life without parole sentence
stories.summary: The Michigan Supreme Court has directed a review of Ethan Crumbley's life without parole sentence for the 2021 Oxford High School shooting.

stories.title: Michigan Supreme Court revives appeal of ‘factory farm’ discharge permit in light of Line 5 ruling
stories.summary: The Michigan Supreme Court has directed the Court of Appeals to reconsider a case involving factory farm discharge permits, citing the recent Line 5 ruling that required stricter environmental review. The court’s decision in the Line 5 tunnel project case has set a precedent that could influence how permits for concentrated animal feeding operations (CAFOs) are evaluated under the Michigan Environmental Protection Act.

photo.alt: Line 5 pipeline and environmental concerns

stories.title: Michigan Supreme Court sends Oxford school shooter case back to appellate court for review
stories.summary: The Michigan Supreme Court has remanded Ethan Crumbley’s case back to the Court of Appeals to review whether a lower court erred in sentencing him to life without parole for the 2021 Oxford High School shooting. Crumbley, who pleaded guilty in 2022 to four murders and seven injuries, had his appeal to withdraw his guilty plea denied in May 2025 for lacking merit. His attorney argued that waiving appellate rights by pleading guilty deprived him of a direct appeal.

photo.alt: Memorial items on the sign of Oxford High School in Oxford, Mich., with dates referencing the 2021 shooting incident.

stories.title: Michigan Tax Tribunal to Hire 2.0 Limited-Term Employees for Small Claims Backlog
stories.summary: The Michigan Tax Tribunal will hire up to 2.0 limited-term employees to address a backlog in small claims cases. Unexpended funds will remain available until project completion by September 30, 2029, with a total estimated cost of $359,300.

stories.title: Michigan Technological University H-STEM Project Cost Reduction
stories.summary: The cost to construct the Michigan Technological University – H-STEM Engineering and Health Technology Complex – Phase I project has been decreased by $1,514,800 to a new total project cost of $51,585,200. The state building authority share is $29,699,800, with the university contributing $21,885,200 and the state general fund/general purpose share at $200.

stories.title: Michigan to Implement Career and Technical Education Reporting Mechanism
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Education will develop a reporting system for school districts to track career and technical education participation and workforce development outcomes. The report will include student participation numbers, high school course enrollment, and postsecondary program enrollment data.

stories.title: Michigan to Publish Literacy Achievement and Opportunity Transparency Dashboard by March 1, 2027
stories.summary: Michigan's legislature mandates the publication of a literacy achievement and opportunity transparency dashboard by March 1, 2027. The dashboard, to be developed by the department in collaboration with the department of lifelong education and the center, will track metrics like pre-K access, educator training in reading science, curriculum usage, and literacy assessment results from M-STEP and SAT tests.

stories.title: Michigan to shoulder 75% of SNAP costs under new federal cuts
stories.summary: New eligibility rules and requirements for SNAP have already caused 150,000 Michiganders to lose benefits, with states required to fund 75% of the program starting October 1st. Over 1.5 million people in Michigan rely on SNAP, as hunger rates rise amid policy changes.

photo.alt: Image related to SNAP policy changes in Michigan

stories.title: Michigan to shoulder 75% of SNAP costs under new federal cuts
stories.summary: New federal SNAP changes expand work requirements, reduce age exemptions, and remove veteran and homelessness exemptions. Starting October 1st, Michigan will cover 75% of SNAP costs as the federal government reduces its funding share. Food pantries like Capuchin Services Center prepare for increased demand due to eligibility restrictions and processing delays.

photo.alt: Michigan to shoulder 75% of SNAP costs under new federal cuts

stories.title: Michigan to Update Dyslexia Handbook Every 5 Years
stories.summary: The state mandates regular reviews and updates of the Michigan Dyslexia Handbook or a similar resource guide, with updates not exceeding a 5-year interval to ensure alignment with current research on dyslexia education.

stories.title: Michigan Townships Association Joins Coalition Opposing Proposal 1 of 2026
stories.summary: The Michigan Townships Association joined a bipartisan coalition urging voters to reject Proposal 1 of 2026, which would initiate a constitutional convention to rewrite Michigan's Constitution.

stories.title: Michigan traffic stops are leading to deportations. This law is a big reason why
stories.summary: Traffic stops in Michigan often lead to deportations due to a law requiring proof of valid immigration status for driver’s licenses. Undocumented immigrants, unable to obtain licenses, face heightened risks of federal immigration enforcement during routine police interactions. A 2025 bill to expand driver’s license eligibility for migrants was rejected, exacerbating tensions between local policing and immigration enforcement.

stories.title: Michigan universities slide in rankings in new national report
stories.summary: The University of Michigan dropped from 20th to 25th in national rankings, with nearly half of 12 listed Michigan institutions seeing declines. Smaller institutions improved their standings, while MIT unseated Princeton as the top-ranked university. The rankings now consider affordability, earnings by major, and post-graduation income levels.

stories.title: Michigan Uses Mobile Dental Permit Fees to Offset Costs
stories.summary: Revenue from mobile dental facility permit fees will be used to offset the costs of processing and issuing permits. This directive is based on public health code provisions.

stories.summary: Michigan’s rural communities are struggling to find people to hold public office. Lansing has been slow to help.

stories.title: Michigan villages have a fix for shortage of officials. Townships can’t use it
stories.summary: Michigan villages can appoint non-resident clerks and treasurers to address staffing shortages, while townships are legally required to elect officials from within their borders. Over 75% of townships and villages struggle to fill mandatory positions, with some facing crises in election management and tax collection. Two bills aimed at easing these issues have stalled in the Legislature.

photo.alt: The Michigan Treasury helped Village of Garden President Jeffrey Lefevre switch the community’s clerk and treasurer jobs from elected to appointed roles.

stories.title: Michigan voters to decide on constitutional convention proposal
stories.summary: Michigan voters will vote on Proposal 1 to decide whether to call a constitutional convention in Lansing. This question appears on the ballot every 16 years since 1978, with past rejections. If approved, a spring election would select delegates for a fall 2027 convention.

stories.title: Michigan voters to decide whether to call a constitutional convention
stories.summary: Supporters of Proposal 1 argue that a new state Constitution could address high taxes, loss of local control over planning and zoning, and unaffordable government. stories.title: Michigan Weather: Below-normal temps will keep a grip until warmup arrives
stories.summary: Michigan is experiencing below-normal temperatures with frost advisories in the Upper Peninsula and northern Lower Peninsula. Highs are expected in the low to mid 60s through Wednesday, with a warmup to the 70s by the weekend. Light rain is possible in southern Michigan, while beach hazards persist along Lake Michigan and Lake Huron.

stories.title: Michigan Weather: Cool, dry air settles in for the week
stories.summary: A mostly dry week with cooler temperatures is expected, with Monday forecast to have the coldest temps and potential frost in parts of the Upper Peninsula and northern Lower Peninsula. Temperatures will remain in the 60s through midweek before gradually warming to the 70s by late week and next weekend. The National Weather Service highlights a cooler, drier pattern from Canadian high pressure, with frost risks and falling humidity creating a fall-like feel.

stories.title: Michigan will be red, orange and yellow soon. 2026 foliage forecast
stories.summary: Michigan's fall foliage in 2026 will feature a range of colors from red, orange, and yellow, depending on the tree species. stories.title: Michigan woman, 63, pleads to 5 charges of sexually assaulting girl she babysat
stories.summary: A 63-year-old Midland County woman pleaded no contest to five counts of second-degree criminal sexual conduct with a relation, resulting in a one-year jail sentence and 25 years of sex offender registration. The charges stem from abuse between 2013 and 2020 when she babysat a girl under 13. Prosecution dismissed 48 other counts in exchange for her plea.

stories.title: Michigan woman accused in $4.6M child modeling scheme sentenced to 5 years in prison
stories.summary: Chanise Coyne, 46, of New Boston, was sentenced to five years in prison for wire fraud related to a $4.6 million scheme involving fictional child modeling events. She also faces paying $4.67 million in restitution and three years of supervised release. Authorities allege she used funds for personal expenses, including Taylor Swift concert tickets and gambling.

stories.title: MichMash: Analyzing Michigan's gubernatorial race ahead of the midterms
stories.summary: With only months until the midterms, Michigan's gubernatorial candidates are seeking support, but the race between Jocelyn Benson and John James is drawing less attention than the U.S. Senate race. Andrea Bitely of Bitely Communications calls it 'the most boring gubernatorial race in history,' noting that Mayor Mike Duggan's May 21, 2026, withdrawal reduced interest. stories.title: Mike Dawes
stories.summary: Mike Dawes, an English guitarist known for composing, arranging, and performing multiple parts simultaneously on a single guitar, is regarded as one of the world’s most creative modern fingerstyle guitarists. stories.title: Mike Dawes to Perform at The Ark

stories.title: Mike Duggan Drops Out of Michigan Governor's Race
stories.summary: Independent candidate Mike Duggan, former Detroit mayor, has withdrawn from the gubernatorial race with less than six months until the midterm elections. Analysts suggest the current political climate made an independent victory unlikely, despite Duggan's perceived electability. The decision impacts both Democratic and Republican reactions as the race narrows.

stories.title: Mike Rogers calls for gas tax pause. It’s a no-go, says state GOP leader
stories.summary: Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers proposed suspending state and federal gas taxes amid rising fuel prices, but Michigan House Speaker Matt Hall, a GOP ally, warned it would jeopardize a bipartisan road funding deal and state budget stability. Gas prices in Michigan have surged to $4.75 per gallon on average, with some stations exceeding $5, as conflicts in the Middle East disrupt oil supplies. Democratic rival Abdul El-Sayed criticized Rogers' proposal, attributing price spikes to the Trump administration's policies.

photo.alt: Michigan’s $4.75-per-gallon average gas price is the 10th highest in the U.S., with some stations in metro Detroit exceeding $5 per gallon.

stories.title: Mike Rogers calls for gas tax pause. It’s a no-go, says state GOP leader

High gas prices in Michigan, currently averaging $4.75 per gallon, have sparked debate over tax suspensions and their impact on infrastructure funding.

stories.title: Mike Rogers Claims He Was An Assembly Line Worker, The UAW Said That Is Stretching The Truth
stories.summary: Mike Rogers claimed he worked as an assembly line worker at Cars & Concepts in Michigan, but the UAW disputes this, stating the facility was an aftermarket shop rather than a traditional assembly line. UAW Local 651 president Art Reyes II emphasized that the work at Cars & Concepts involved modifying pre-built vehicles, not building them from scratch, and criticized Rogers for misrepresenting his experience to connect with Michiganders' automotive heritage.

stories.title: Mike Rogers has a new position on the Iran war. Again.

His evolving positions include calling for an end date amid rising gas prices and affordability concerns, despite earlier claims it should be 'conditional' without a fixed timeline. Rogers now faces scrutiny for aligning with Trump's war while distancing from its economic consequences.

stories.title: Mike Rogers voted against children’s health coverage over and over
stories.summary: Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers repeatedly voted against expanding health insurance for low-income children, opposing legislation that Michigan officials said could help tens of thousands of uninsured kids get medical care. Between 2004 and 2009, the then-congressman cast 19 votes against measures to extend, expand, or increase funding for the State Children’s Health Insurance Program. The program aimed to cover children in working families who earned too much for Medicaid but not enough for private insurance.

stories.title: Milford horse stable owner files lawsuit against Oakland County for ‘unlawful’ search and seizure

The investigation, which began in July 2026, followed complaints from former employees about neglect and abuse at High Vibe Trails, including underweight horses, lack of veterinary care, and unsafe conditions. stories.title: MLive announces its print newspapers will move fully online starting in December
stories.summary: MLive has announced that all of its print newspapers will be discontinued and moved fully online, with the final print editions published on December 6, 2026. The decision follows data showing digital subscriptions have surpassed print, and the company emphasizes the move is to better serve readers and communities. MLive will not lay off newsroom staff and acknowledges some readers may not transition to digital due to lack of internet access.

stories.title: 'Money out of politics': Understanding Proposal 2 on Michigan November 2026 ballot
stories.summary: Proposal 2 on the 2026 Michigan ballot seeks to ban campaign contributions from regulated utilities and government contractors with large contracts, and expand campaign finance regulations to include more political communications, requiring donor disclosures. The proposal would prohibit contributions from utilities and contractors with over $250,000 in government contracts, and apply campaign finance laws to additional political communications including internet-based ones.

photo.alt: 'Money out of politics': Understanding Proposal 2 on Michigan November 2026 ballot

stories.title: 'Money out of politics': Understanding Proposal 2 on Michigan November 2026 ballot
stories.summary: Michigan voters will decide Proposal 2, a campaign finance regulation initiative, on Nov. 3, 2026. It would also expand regulations to cover political communications identifying candidates or ballot questions.

stories.title: More DPSCD schools have air conditioning, but many are still without it

While portable units and fans are being distributed, many educators and staff still report inadequate cooling. The district plans to address bus route coordination challenges by 2027 to allow A/C-equipped schools to remain open on hot days.

stories.title: More focus on career pathways for high schoolers

The initiative includes smaller class sizes, additional tutoring for literacy support, and hiring seven more counselors to achieve a 1:250 student-to-counselor ratio. Superintendent Nikolai Vitti emphasized reducing credit deficits to enable college and career course access by 11th grade.

stories.title: Near Sleeping Bear Dunes, residents battle beavers — and feds — over floods

A $1.1 million culvert project and studies show dam removal can significantly lower lake levels, yet the park maintains a cautious approach requiring data-driven justification for interventions.

stories.title: Paris Hilton-backed bill limiting youth transport restraints heads to governor’s desk
stories.summary: A Michigan House bill prohibiting the use of certain restraints by youth transport companies to residential treatment facilities has passed the Senate and is now awaiting Governor Gretchen Whitmer's signature. Sponsored by Rep. The bill also bans overnight pickups and imposes $1,000 civil fines for violations.

stories.title: Police seize 2 hand grenades from deceased Hemlock resident’s home
stories.summary: Police have seized a pair of hand grenades from a Hemlock-area home. Richland Township police learned of the two potential explosive weapons at a residence in the 300 block Sandridge Drive on Thursday, Sept. 17. Officers who initially inspected the grenades believed one was decommissioned while the other appeared to be live. Officers summoned a member from the Michigan State Police Bomb Squad to the scene. The trooper confirmed both grenades were live and operable.

stories.title: Poll: Trust in the U.S. Postal Service delivering mail-in ballots on time has fallen

stories.title: Proposal 1: Rewrite Michigan's Constitution: Here's How It Would Work
stories.summary: Michigan's constitution could be rewritten through a convention if voters approve Proposal 1. The process involves electing delegates, convening in October, and submitting proposed changes for approval. Historical records show the 1961 convention took 500 hours and generated over 800 proposals. A 2026 convention could cost $80 million, requiring legislative funding and addressing election logistics and delegate regulations.

photo.alt: Proposal 1: Rewrite Michigan's Constitution: Here's How It Would Work

stories.title: Proposal 1: Rewrite Michigan’s Constitution? Here’s how it would work
stories.summary: Michigan voters will decide in November 2026 whether to rewrite the state Constitution via Proposal 1. If approved, the measure would trigger a constitutional convention to elect 148 delegates who would draft a new constitution for voter approval. Supporters argue it could address government gridlock, while opponents warn it risks undoing recent voter-approved protections like abortion rights and redistricting reforms.

stories.title: Report says Trump Medicaid work requirements won't lead to more employment

stories.title: REQUIRE SCIENCE OF READING TO BE PART OF TEACHER PREPARATION PROGRAMS

Programs must ensure instructors have comprehensive knowledge of reading science for certification eligibility.

stories.title: Rural Michigan leaders push back against data center boom as election looms
stories.summary: A survey by the University of Michigan reveals that less than 1 in 5 Michigan local government officials believe large-scale data centers are worth their costs, with rural leaders most skeptical. The backlash against data centers, initially seen as economic boons, has led to proposed halts and regulatory discussions, with both gubernatorial candidates calling for moratoriums. Over 60% of residents oppose data center construction, making it a key issue in the upcoming midterm elections.

photo.alt: Rural Michigan leaders push back against data center boom as election looms

stories.title: Rural townships squeezed on all sides in Michigan, as money woes mount
stories.summary: Rural townships in Michigan are facing severe financial strain due to tax restraints, inflation, and cumbersome grant processes, leading to service cuts and infrastructure neglect. A recent survey shows declining fiscal health in these communities, with local officials calling for increased state assistance and simplified grant procedures.

stories.title: Rural townships squeezed on all sides in Michigan, as money woes mount
stories.summary: Rural leaders in Michigan report unprecedented financial stress due to tax restraints, inflation, and complex grant applications, leading to service cuts. A statewide survey shows fewer than half of rural communities report good fiscal health, the lowest in a decade. Townships struggle with aging infrastructure, limited staffing, and inadequate funding despite state assistance programs.

stories.title: Rural women who got C-sections more likely to be prescribed opioids at home, study finds
stories.summary: Women giving birth in rural communities were more likely than urban peers to receive oral opioid prescriptions after a cesarean section, according to a study analyzing 540,000 C-sections. The analysis found rural women also received more acetaminophen and NSAIDs post-discharge, raising concerns about opioid use amid the national epidemic and maternal health risks.

stories.title: Saginaw council approves data center ordinance after months of planning
stories.summary: Saginaw City Council unanimously approved a data center development ordinance on Sept. 28, 2026, set to take effect Oct. 9. The policy establishes zoning regulations, environmental protections, and community engagement requirements for data centers. The ordinance follows a 2026 moratorium on such developments and addresses national concerns about data center impacts.

stories.title: Saginaw credit union executive fired over Lake America photo. Here's why

Smith stated the post was not intended as a political statement but to humorously comment on the name change, which sparked controversy. The credit union appointed Jason Acosta as interim CEO and expressed commitment to community trust.

stories.title: Saginaw man, 71, charged with drunkenly crashing into stopped Michigan State Police vehicle
stories.summary: A Saginaw man has been charged with a felony two months after allegedly drunkenly crashing into a Michigan State Police patrol vehicle. Prosecutors on Sept. 8 issued a warrant for the 71-year-old man, charging him with third-offense operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated and driving with an open alcohol container. The first charge is a five-year felony, while the second is a 90-day misdemeanor.

Police pursued the suspect following a domestic dispute, leading to a crash near Linwood. He faces a $750,000 bond and has a prior felony firearm conviction.

stories.title: Saginaw man gets prison time for stabbing, trying to kill man at East Side gas station
stories.summary: A Saginaw man is prison-bound for repeatedly stabbing and trying to kill a man at an East Side gas station in an apparent dispute over childcare. Saginaw County Circuit Judge Darnell Jackson on Thursday, Sept. 17, sentenced 52-year-old Donald A. Williams to five to 15 years in prison. He gave Williams credit for 301 days already served in the county jail and ordered him to pay $198 in fines and costs.

stories.title: Saginaw man pleads guilty to child abuse for ‘whooping’ minor over sexual orientation
stories.summary: A Saginaw man, Tony H. Morgan, 53, pleaded guilty to third-degree child abuse for allegedly beating an underage girl with a belt because she identified as gay. Prosecutors stated Morgan forced the girl to undress, struck her repeatedly, and made derogatory remarks about her sexual orientation. As part of a plea deal, Morgan will receive probation and must complete a parenting class.

photo.alt: Saginaw County Circuit Judge Darnell Jackson is seen in this file photo.

stories.title: Saginaw Township schools weigh engineering fixes to address Arrowwood flooding
stories.summary: Saginaw Township Community Schools officials will consider engineering solutions to address recurring flooding issues at Arrowwood Elementary School, which was closed for a week in April 2026 and several days in 2013. Superintendent Jamie Kraatz stated that while recent work has cleared drainage blockages, heavy rainfall exceeding 3-4 inches in 24 hours could still cause water accumulation, prompting plans for a retention pond and parking lot re-engineering.

SAT results also increased, with 35.1% of students meeting English benchmarks and 15.7% in math. The district attributes progress to smaller class sizes and interventions for ninth graders, while a recent analysis highlights DPSCD as a top-performing district in student learning speed.

photo.alt: The Detroit school district continues long-term improvement on 2026 M-STEP results

stories.title: The Detroit school district continues long-term improvement on 2026 M-STEP results
stories.summary: Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) attributes recent academic improvements to investments in teacher recruitment, evidence-based curriculum, student interventions, and wraparound services. The district has used funds from a $94.4 million literacy lawsuit settlement to hire academic interventionists and expand tutoring, though budget challenges loom as those funds expire. Chronic absenteeism has also declined since pandemic-era closures, contributing to better student outcomes.

photo.alt: The Detroit school district continues long-term improvement on 2026 M-STEP results

stories.summary: In Michigan, we vote for the people who oversee three of our public universities. Each university also uses a different word for the same role. stories.title: The Mids: University governing boards on your ballot?
stories.summary: Michigan voters elect members of governing boards for three public universities (University of Michigan, Michigan State University, and Wayne State University) using different titles for the same role. This system is unique to Michigan, with elections decided via statewide citizen vote rather than regional or appointed methods. The practice stems from Jacksonian democracy principles in the state Constitution but faces criticism for lack of transparency in candidate selection.

stories.title: This Jackson bike shop sharpened skates, fixed flats - and lasted 75 years
stories.summary: Barber's Bike Shop in Jackson, Michigan, closed after 75 years in business. stories.summary: Trinity Health, headquartered in Livonia, will permanently lay off 557 employees primarily in IT support starting October 25 and continuing through November 29. The layoffs follow a decision to outsource technology services, but a law firm is investigating potential violations of the WARN Act due to a 60-day notice period discrepancy.

stories.title: Trinity Health layoffs expose the danger of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act
stories.summary: Trinity Health in Livonia, Michigan announced 557 layoffs linked to federal Medicare and Medicaid cuts from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA). The law has already put 23 Michigan healthcare providers at risk and is projected to strip 171,000-355,000 residents of health coverage. Republican lawmakers including Senate candidate Mike Rogers and Michigan's congressional delegation supported the legislation despite its negative impacts.

photo.alt: Trinity Health layoffs in Livonia, Michigan

stories.summary: The museum won Tripadvisor’s 'Travelers’ Choice Award 2024', placing it in the top 10% of worldwide attractions based on millions of reviews.

stories.title: Trump administration revokes $810M approved by Congress for refugee aid and more
stories.summary: The Trump administration has revoked $810 million in refugee aid approved by Congress, among other actions. The decision impacts funding allocated for refugee support programs.

stories.title: Trump Administration Rolls Back Power Plant Emission Rules
stories.summary: The Trump administration announced it will roll back rules governing power plant emissions, despite scientific consensus on climate change. Rachel Rothschild, an assistant professor at Michigan Law, discusses the implications of this decision.

stories.title: Trump administration says developers, loggers can kill endangered species
stories.summary: The Trump administration’s top wildlife official issued a directive expanding rollbacks of endangered species protections, allowing developers and loggers to kill endangered animals if the activity’s purpose is not to kill them. Wildlife advocates warn this undermines the Endangered Species Act, creating loopholes for habitat destruction and accidental harm. Legal challenges and debates over the law’s interpretation are expected to intensify.

photo.alt: Endangered species and logging activities

stories.title: Trump DOJ uses case of Utah letter carrier to highlight allegations of voting fraud
stories.summary: The Trump Department of Justice highlighted a Utah letter carrier case to emphasize allegations of voting fraud, while a federal court blocked a Postal Service rule that aimed to affect election policies. The Supreme Court upheld the decision, arguing the rule was an attempt to influence elections rather than a modest mail regulation.

photo.alt: Trump DOJ uses case of Utah letter carrier to highlight allegations of voting fraud

stories.title: Trump launches campaign tour in GOP-friendly states ahead of midterms
stories.summary: Donald Trump has launched a campaign tour in GOP-friendly states as part of efforts to energize the Republican base ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. The tour focuses on key battleground states where the party aims to maintain control of Congress.

photo.alt: Trump launches campaign tour in GOP-friendly states ahead of midterms

stories.title: Trump likes data centers. Congress seems stuck. The midterms could deliver a verdict.
stories.summary: The House passed a bill requiring states to consider data centers paying for electricity costs, but Senate action is stalled. Trump opposes restrictions, and the issue is a key topic in midterm races with bipartisan opposition to data centers.
