stories.title: Trump lowers fuel economy standards. Detroit automakers welcome change
stories.summary: The Trump administration introduced relaxed fuel economy standards, which Detroit automakers support but environmental groups criticize. The new rules reduce requirements for vehicle efficiency, aligning with Trump's opposition to electric vehicle incentives. The standards project a 2031 fleet average of 34.9 mpg, down from Biden-era projections, and are expected to lower vehicle costs while increasing carbon emissions.

photo.alt: Unsold 2026 F-150 pickup trucks sit in a long line outside a Ford dealership on April 12, 2026, in Centennial, Colo.

stories.title: Trump lowers fuel economy standards. Detroit automakers welcome change
stories.summary: The Trump administration has finalized new fuel economy standards that relax requirements for automakers, reducing the mandated mileage compared to previous projections. The change aligns with Trump’s campaign to roll back policies favoring electric vehicles, potentially increasing vehicle affordability but also exposing Americans to more pollution. The decision follows tensions with Iran over the Strait of Hormuz, which impacted oil prices.

photo.alt: Donald Trump speaks during an event on fuel economy standards in the Oval Office of the White House, Dec. 3, 2025, in Washington. (AP Photo/Evan Vucci, File)

stories.title: Trump PAC helps drive Michigan Senate race toward record spending
stories.summary: Michigan’s US Senate race between Republican Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed is on pace to be the most expensive in state history, with over $205 million in disclosed spending and an additional $65 million in reserved ads through Election Day. Trump-aligned super PACs like Senate Leadership Fund and No Going Back have driven GOP spending to $59.3 million, while Democrats have spent $23 million in disclosed campaign funds and $43.8 million in ads, including dark money. The race remains competitive with El-Sayed leading polls by 3.5 points and the Cook Political Report rating it a toss-up.

photo.alt: Mike Rogers and Abdul El-Sayed in a split image

stories.title: Trump PAC helps drive Michigan Senate race toward record spending
stories.summary: Michigan's U.S. Senate race between Mike Rogers and Abdul El-Sayed is on track to be the most expensive in state history, with over $205 million in disclosed spending and an additional $65 million in reserved ads. The race includes significant contributions from dark money groups, which do not disclose their donors, and is being heavily influenced by Republican-aligned super PACs, including those linked to Donald Trump.

photo.alt: Mike Rogers and Abdul El-Sayed in a split image

stories.title: Trump pushes daylight saving; clocks expected to change
stories.summary: Daylight saving time ends at 2 a.m. local time on Sunday, Nov. 1, when clocks move back one hour to 1 a.m. The shift marks the return to standard time and gives Americans an extra hour of sleep, while also bringing earlier sunsets and more morning daylight through the winter months.

stories.title: Trump renames Lake Ontario to Lake America. What does Ontario mean?
stories.summary: The article explains the historical and Indigenous origins of the names of three Great Lakes: Lake Superior (named by French settlers as 'Le Lac Superior' meaning upper lake), Lake Michigan (derived from the Indigenous name Michigami), and Lake Huron (named after the Huron-Wendat people, previously called 'La Mer Douce' by French settlers).

stories.title: Trump's clock plan could affect Halloween

Gretchen Whitmer, and Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson. Both face multiple felony charges with potential decades-long prison sentences.

stories.title: U-M study paves way to negate pollution from nitrates
stories.summary: A University of Michigan study led by Professor Nathaniel Szymczak has developed a catalytic system to convert environmentally harmful nitrates into reusable compounds. The research, published in 'Nature Chemistry', addresses nitrate pollution caused by agricultural runoff, which leads to algal blooms and ecosystem disruption. The team studied biological enzymes to create a chemical process that mimics natural nitrate reduction methods.

The investigation revealed a sophisticated operation involving multiple inmates and associates, with contraband including K2, high-potency THC wax, and suboxone strips. MDOC Director Heidi E. Washington emphasized the dangers of contraband entering facilities and the collaboration with law enforcement to hold suspects accountable.

stories.title: Vitti, board members consider summer school changes
stories.summary: Detroit Public Schools Community District leaders and board members are discussing potential changes to summer school, including mandatory attendance for students significantly behind grade level and shifting focus toward academic remediation. stories.summary: Detroit Public Schools Community District leaders are considering mandatory summer school for students significantly behind grade level, with board members suggesting changes like paying students to attend and refocusing programs on academics. stories.title: Voices: $5 gas isn’t just a price spike. It’s a warning.
stories.summary: Michigan drivers face $5 gas prices, highlighting systemic oil dependence that strains budgets and drives inflation. photo.alt: Voices: $5 gas isn’t just a price spike. It’s a warning.

stories.title: Voices: Michigan PFAS Awareness Week is a call to action
stories.summary: Michigan's PFAS Awareness Week (Sept. 21-25, 2026) highlights the state's ongoing battle with per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) contamination in water, soil, and communities. The article connects historical PFAS pollution from military bases, manufacturing, and airports to new threats from data center expansion, which uses PFAS in cooling systems. Advocates call for stronger regulations and corporate accountability to address this public health crisis.

photo.alt: Image related to PFAS contamination and environmental concerns

stories.title: Voices: The PFAS rollback is not the whole problem
stories.summary: The article argues that while the EPA's recent PFAS regulation rollback is harmful, the deeper issue is that federal law has only ever regulated a tiny fraction (0.0429% before the rollback, 0.0143% after) of the 14,000+ PFAS chemicals. It emphasizes the need for class-wide regulation to address PFAS contamination's widespread health and environmental impacts.

photo.alt: Voices: The PFAS rollback is not the whole problem

stories.title: Volunteers removed 4,000 pounds of trash from Kalamazoo River during cleanup day
stories.summary: More than 250 volunteers removed over 4,000 pounds of trash from the Kalamazoo River during the third annual cleanup event on June 20, 2026. The effort, which spanned 10 miles of the river and involved canoe/kayak crews, was recognized with the Rotary District 6360 Foundation Golden Trowel Award on August 24, 2026. Organizers aim to expand the 2027 event with greater community and youth involvement.

stories.summary: Thirty-four Detroiters are running for five seats on the Detroit Public Schools Community District. stories.summary: Voters in midterm elections are blaming President Donald Trump’s tariffs for rising living costs, with families like Rebecca Myers’ in Virginia forgoing vacations to save money. Public opinion surveys show growing anger over affordability, and organizers are targeting key congressional districts to highlight tariff impacts. Economists estimate tariffs have added hundreds of dollars to household expenses, with states like Michigan and Florida facing billions in added costs.

stories.summary: Voters in several Washtenaw County cities and townships will decide on multiple ballot proposals on Nov. 3, 2026, including Ann Arbor's potential city-run electric utility, property tax levies, and election rule changes. stories.summary: Detroit is upgrading hundreds of bus stops with new shelters and benches to improve the public transportation experience. The Detroit Department of Transportation plans to install 210 shelters and 200 benches by 2027, funded through grants and city funds. The project, part of DDOT Reimagined, prioritizes high-ridership stops and includes partnerships for shelter maintenance and advertising.

stories.summary: Walmart's annual fall sale event in October offers major discounts on home, fashion, and technology products in Michigan. The sale coincides with holiday shopping preparations. Target and Amazon Prime also have events around the same dates.

stories.title: Warren double homicide from 1981 reopened, but evidence was destroyed
stories.summary: Warren police have reopened a 1981 double homicide case involving Cheryl Kemp and Lisa Schwartzkopf, but physical evidence from the crime was destroyed or released decades ago. Families of the victims are seeking closure as detectives use modern DNA technology to re-examine the cold case. The original evidence included bullets, clothing, and biological samples, with some items sent to the Michigan State Police lab before being lost in an inventory error.

stories.title: Warren flea market vendor killed after dispute over refund, police say
stories.summary: Mirhad Cehic, 57, was killed after a dispute over a refund at a Warren flea market. Police say a van struck him following an argument with two customers. A Detroit man has been charged with murder in the incident.

stories.title: Warren man fatally struck while teaching daughter to drive, police say
stories.summary: A 62-year-old Warren man was fatally struck by his 18-year-old daughter during a parallel parking lesson on Sunday afternoon. The crash occurred in the 24000 block of Warner Avenue around 4 p.m., with emergency responders transporting him to a hospital where he later died. Police state drugs and alcohol were not factors, and the daughter is cooperating with investigators.

photo.alt: Jenny Sherman headshot

stories.title: Warren Parks Commission Seeks Additional Sponsorships for Drone Show
stories.summary: The Parks and Recreation Commission discussed sponsorship support for event expenses and identified a need for additional funding to proceed with an advertised drone show. Commissioners recommended pursuing more local business sponsorships to address the funding gap.

stories.title: Washtenaw Business Lens: How AI is transforming the way people do business
stories.summary: Jonah Bailey and Andy LaBarre discuss AI's impact on industries like manufacturing, healthcare, and software, emphasizing the need for guardrails, ethical considerations, and the urgency for businesses to adapt. They highlight challenges in customer behavior prediction, data center sustainability, and AI-generated content transparency.

photo.alt: Jonah Bailey discussing AI in business

stories.title: Washtenaw Community College to host career fair with 70 employers
stories.summary: Washtenaw Community College will host its Fall Career and Internship Fair on October 26, featuring around 70 employers from diverse sectors including healthcare, IT, and manufacturing. The free event includes workshops for job seekers and pre-registration is encouraged.

stories.summary: Washtenaw County’s Office for Community and Economic Development awarded $40,000 to nine local businesses as part of the Mini Grant Program in 2026.

stories.title: Washtenaw County Health Department Encourages Restaurants to Join Restaurant Meal Program
stories.summary: The Washtenaw County Health Department is encouraging local restaurants to join the Restaurant Meal Program, which allows eligible individuals to use SNAP benefits for ready-to-go meals. Eight restaurants, including Subway locations and Stimulatte Cafe, currently participate. The program aims to increase access for vulnerable populations like the elderly, disabled, and homeless by providing meals without requiring cooking equipment.

stories.summary: The Washtenaw County Health Department will host an evening flu clinic for children and families on Oct. 13, 2026. Walk-ins are welcome, but appointments have priority. The health department will not turn anyone away due to financial situation.

stories.summary: The Washtenaw County Health Department provides walk-in flu vaccinations on Mondays and Wednesdays at 555 Towner St., Ypsilanti. Appointments can also be scheduled by phone. The department will not deny vaccines due to financial situation.

stories.title: Washtenaw County Sheriff’s Department keeps peace between ICE and observers in Ypsilanti Township
stories.summary: The Washtenaw County Sheriff’s Office responded to 911 calls in Ypsilanti Township to de-escalate tensions between ICE agents and local observers during an arrest at a Speedway gas station. Sheriff Alyshia Dyer stated that deputies arrived as ICE requested assistance due to a crowd blocking their vehicles, leading to the situation being calmed and ICE agents leaving the scene.

photo.alt: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents and local observers at a Speedway gas station in Ypsilanti Township.

stories.title: Washtenaw County weighs landfill expansion, Northville residents object
stories.summary: Northville Township residents oppose GFL’s proposed Arbor Hills Landfill expansion in Salem Township due to past pollution and unapproved height increases. Washtenaw County is weighing waste reduction against landfill space needs, with further discussion scheduled for Nov. 18.

photo.alt: Washtenaw County weighs landfill expansion, Northville residents object

stories.title: Washtenaw Housing Alliance introduces the 'Yvonne Fund' to assist those assisting the homeless
stories.summary: The Yvonne Fund, a permanent endowment, provides ongoing financial support for permanent supportive housing services in Washtenaw County. By distributing annual grants to organizations like Avalon Housing and Michigan Ability Partners, the fund aims to reduce reliance on yearly fundraising and ensure long-term stability for housing initiatives. The model has already supported 65 housing units in 2026 through $326,000 in grants.

photo.alt: A general image related to housing initiatives

stories.title: Washtenaw United: Ann Arbor Area Community Foundation continues its philanthropy in uncertain times
stories.summary: The Ann Arbor Area Community Foundation discusses its community-driven grant-making process, local impact investing strategies, and the generational impact of scholarships. Shannon Polk highlights how community members review applications, data-informed decisions, and stories of scholarship recipients transforming lives in Washtenaw County.

stories.title: Washtenaw United: SafeHouse Center continues to serve those recovering from domestic violence with help from the community
stories.summary: SafeHouse Center's Executive Director Christine Watson discusses the organization's role in supporting domestic violence survivors, challenges with affordable housing, and the importance of community partnerships. Watson emphasizes the need for continued investment in resources to ensure survivors can transition safely from temporary shelter to stable housing and community integration.

photo.alt: Christine Watson, Executive Director of SafeHouse Center

stories.title: Washtenaw United: United Way for Southeastern Michigan works to prepare grants for its partners that serve the community
stories.summary: United Way for Southeastern Michigan evaluates grant impact through mid-year and final reports, with 72% of funds used for staff salaries and benefits. Organizations face challenges like funding cuts and burnout, but collaboration among service providers is growing. The partnership with WEMU explores community investments in equity and opportunity.

stories.title: Washtenaw United: United Way for Southeastern Michigan presents Power of the Purse 2026
stories.summary: United Way for Southeastern Michigan's Power of the Purse 2026 event focuses on supporting women's financial stability and independence. Senior Director Katie Groves discusses the initiative's role in providing grants to women-led organizations, addressing systemic barriers, and offering wraparound services to over 424 families in Washtenaw County. The event highlights the historical struggle for women's financial autonomy, tracing back to the 1974 Equal Credit Opportunity Act.

photo.alt: Washtenaw United: United Way for Southeastern Michigan presents Power of the Purse 2026

stories.summary: Wayne County Prosecutor Kym Worthy announced charges against the suspect accused of fatally shooting three people and wounding four others at an illicit after-hours party on Detroit's west side. stories.title: Wayne County judge Cusick dismisses Detroit Tenants Union lawsuit
stories.summary: A Wayne County judge dismissed the Detroit Tenants Union's lawsuit against the 36th District Court. The union claimed judges allowed landlords to collect rent or evict tenants from properties lacking city-issued certificates of compliance. The dismissal follows Mayor Mary Sheffield's announcement to bring thousands of rental properties up to code within a year.

stories.title: Wayne County landfill’s lawyers say radioactive waste ban ‘judicial overreach’
stories.summary: Wayne Disposal is appealing a permanent injunction that blocks radioactive waste shipments to its Van Buren Township landfill, arguing the judge's decision represents 'judicial overreach' based on potential future risks rather than present harm. The landfill's lawyers claim health risks from the waste are 'functionally zero' and that the ruling undermines interstate commerce and waste management protocols. Communities and environmental groups had sued to prevent the waste from being transported to the site, citing environmental justice concerns and proximity to densely populated areas.

stories.summary: The Wayne-Westland Community Schools district is implementing a new policy requiring students to keep personal electronic devices put away during instructional time to reduce distractions and enhance learning. stories.summary: The Muslim Student Association at WCC hosted a Ramadan Annual Iftar event to foster community, educate students about the holy month, and bridge connections between Muslim and non-Muslim students. stories.summary: West Michigan Regional Airport has secured a $152,540 grant from the Michigan Department of Transportation to enhance safety operations through updated runway markings and snow removal equipment. stories.title: ‘What environmental racism looks like’: Protest targets University of Michigan computing center
stories.summary: University of Michigan Regent Paul Brown joined a protest against a $1.25-billion data center project in Ypsilanti Township, criticizing the university's lack of community engagement and environmental impact concerns. The facility, described as a 'hyperscale' data center, has faced opposition from residents, officials, and labor groups who argue it will burden the community with costs and environmental risks without providing substantial local benefits. Ypsilanti Township has passed multiple resolutions against the project and is exploring legal options to block it.

stories.title: Ypsilanti City Council fails to pass resolution opposing police budget ballot proposal
stories.summary: A resolution opposing Proposal B on the Ypsilanti November ballot, which would require a public vote to increase the city’s police budget, failed to secure the required majority during a 3-2 council vote. Council members expressed divided opinions, with some arguing the proposal could harm police morale and others questioning the need for voter approval given existing budget processes. Mayor Nicole Brown and Councilmember Me’Chelle King were absent at a conference.

stories.title: Ypsilanti officials consider data center ordinance proposal
stories.summary: The City of Ypsilanti is evaluating a proposed ordinance to update zoning laws for data centers, presented by City Planner Josh Burns on Sept. 15. The proposal includes categorizing data centers by size, setting energy and water consumption limits, and establishing noise and environmental regulations. Councilors discussed concerns about noise, health impacts, and water usage, with the city planning to enforce standards for setbacks, lot coverage, and cooling systems.
